definition_zh: 喷出；涌出（短时间）；喷射；猛增；骤长；一股；一阵
definition_en: to burst or shoot out suddenly for a short time, often in a strong stream
core_image: 瓶口被挤压，一股水突然飞快地喷出来
scene: 水管被踩到，一股水从接口处往外溅。Someone stepped on the hose and water spurted from the joint.
sceneCN: 这里 spurt 是「喷出」（第 1 个义项：液体短促有力地涌出来）；句意：有人踩到了水管，水从接头处喷了出来。

pos.zh: 一股；一阵；喷射；短期的猛增

collocations.zh: 一阵一阵地；断断续续地

derivatives.zh: 由 spurt 加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「喷出的；被喷溅的」
由 spurt 加 -ing 构成，义为「喷出的动作；喷射」
spurt 的复数名词形式，义为「一股股；一阵阵；多段猛增」

senses.title: To burst out in a short stream
senses.definition: to flow or burst out suddenly in a short, strong stream, said of liquids
senses.definitionCN: 液体突然、短促而有力地涌出或喷射出来
senses.example: Blood spurted from the small cut on his thumb.
senses.exampleCN: 血从他拇指上的小伤口喷了出来。
senses.why: The word began as plain English spurten, to squirt, so the core body of the word is the sudden short burst of liquid.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是英语本族的 spurten，意为喷射，所以词的核心就是液体短促有力的一下。

senses.title: To send something out in bursts
senses.definition: to make a liquid or a gas shoot out quickly, often from a container or a broken part
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或气体快速喷出，常来自容器或破损处
senses.example: The pump spurted fuel all over the garage floor.
senses.exampleCN: 泵把燃油喷得车库地面到处都是。
senses.why: The transitive verb simply points the burst at its source, naming the thing that forces the stream out.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法只是把「喷」对准了源头，说出是谁把那股液体逼了出来。

senses.title: A short burst of liquid
senses.definition: a sudden short stream or flow of liquid or gas
senses.definitionCN: 液体或气体突然而短促的一股
senses.example: A spurt of steam rose from the kettle lid.
senses.exampleCN: 壶盖处冒起一股蒸汽。
senses.why: The noun names one single burst, which is why we count these events and speak of a spurt of water or steam.
senses.whyCN: 名词义指单独的一下，所以我们可以数出一股一股，说 a spurt of water 或 steam。

senses.title: To increase quickly for a short time
senses.definition: to rise or grow very quickly in a short period, especially of prices, numbers, or growth
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内快速上升或增长，尤指价格、数字或增长
senses.example: The company saw its orders spurt after the ad campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 广告投放后，这家公司的订单猛增。
senses.why: A liquid stream that shoots up and stops looks like a sharp rise followed by a level, so spurt now describes short bursts of growth.
senses.whyCN: 一股冲上去又停住的液流很像陡然上升后趋于平缓，于是 spurt 用来形容短期的猛增。

senses.title: A sudden short effort of energy
senses.definition: a short, strong effort of energy at the end of a race or a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或工作末尾突然使出的一股短促力量
senses.example: The runner made a final spurt in the last fifty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 那名赛跑选手在最后五十米来了一次冲刺。
senses.why: Energy leaves a body the way water leaves a pipe, so a quick burst of effort is called a spurt.
senses.whyCN: 力气离开身体的方式就像水离开管子，所以短促的一使劲就叫 spurt。

senses.title: In intermittent bursts
senses.definition: used in the phrase in spurts, meaning happening in short bursts rather than steadily
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in spurts，表示一阵一阵地发生，而不是持续稳定地发生
senses.example: She wrote her essay in spurts between other jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 她是在其他事情的间隙里，一阵一阵地写完论文的。
senses.why: If each burst is short, then an activity made of many bursts happens irregularly, which gives us the phrase in spurts.
senses.whyCN: 既然每一下都很短，由许多下组成的活动自然就不规律，这就给出了 in spurts 的说法。

intro.en: Spurt appears in England in its early form spurten, a plain English word for to squirt or to spit.
intro.cn: spurt 约在十七世纪前以 spurten 的形式出现在英格兰，是英语本族词，意为喷射或吐出。

items.en: Spurten is recorded meaning to squirt or to eject liquid in a short stream.
items.cn: 有记录显示 spurten 表示喷射，或说短促有力地把液体挤出来。

items.en: It is related to German spritzen and Dutch spruiten, verbs of spouting and bursting out.
items.cn: 它与德语 spritzen、荷兰语 spruiten 同源，都是喷出、迸出的动词。

items.en: The shorter form spurt appears and is used both as a verb and as a noun for one burst of liquid.
items.cn: 更短的 spurt 出现，既作动词，也作名词指一股液体。

items.en: Spurt grows in sport reports for a short fast effort, and the phrase final spurt becomes common.
items.cn: 在体育报道里 spurt 用来指短促地加速，final spurt 这一说法流行起来。

items.en: Growth spurt spreads in child health writing from the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪初起，growth spurt 在儿童健康读物中流行开来。

items.en: Business pages borrow the word for prices and orders that rise in short sharp jumps.
items.cn: 商业版面又借用这个词，形容价格和订单短期急升。

note.en: Spurt looks like spur and sport, and it sits beside gush and jet as a word for liquid that comes out fast.
note.cn: spurt 与 spur、sport 拼写相近，作为形容液体快速冲出的词，又与 gush、jet 相邻。

entries.definition: a sharp point used to urge a horse forward, or to encourage
entries.definitionCN: 马刺；激励。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an activity done for exercise and fun
entries.definitionCN: 体育运动。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: burst out in a short stream, past tense
entries.definitionCN: 喷出了（过去式）

entries.definition: to flow out suddenly and in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 涌出；喷出（量大）

entries.definition: a strong narrow stream of liquid or gas
entries.definitionCN: 喷射流；射流

entries.definition: to break open or come out suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 爆破；迸发

normalIntro.en: Spurt is a short, sharp push of liquid or effort: picture the word spurring a stream forward.
normalIntro.cn: spurt 是液体或力气短促有力的一下：把它想成在水流后面加了一鞭。

normal.en: Spurt out is the easiest phrase to keep in mind.
normal.cn: spurt out 是最容易记住的搭配。

normal.en: Growth spurt describes the fast few months when children shoot up.
normal.cn: growth spurt 指孩子个子飞快蹿高的那几个月。

normal.en: Final spurt means the last push of a race.
normal.cn: final spurt 指比赛最后的冲刺。

normal.en: In spurts means not steadily, but in fits and starts.
normal.cn: in spurts 表示不是稳定持续，而是一阵一阵地。

normal.en: Compare gush: a gush is long and heavy, a spurt is short and sudden.
normal.cn: 对比 gush：涌出又长又猛，喷射又短又急。

abstract.en: To remember the liquid sense, see a hose with the water pushed out in a thin rope.
abstract.cn: 记「喷出」义时，想象水管被压住，水成一股细线冲出来。

abstract.en: To remember the fast growth sense, see a chart line shooting straight up, then flattening.
abstract.cn: 记「猛增」义时，想象图表曲线直冲上去，然后变平。

abstract.en: To remember the effort sense, see a runner holding back, then firing rounds in the last stride.
abstract.cn: 记「冲刺」义时，想象跑者一直忍着，最后一跃把劲儿全放出来。

examples.en: Lemon juice spurted across the table when she squeezed too hard.
examples.cn: 她挤得太用力，柠檬汁喷得满桌都是。

examples.en: Wages spurted briefly before settling at a higher level.
examples.cn: 工资短暂猛增，之后稳定在一个较高的水平。

examples.en: He does not train every day, but sometimes he will spurt ahead at the finish.
examples.cn: 他并不天天训练，但有时会在终点前猛冲一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死噗特」——水压一紧，噗地一声特猛地喷出；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本族词 spurten（喷射、迸出），与德语 spritzen、荷兰语 spruiten 同源 → 十七世纪写作 spurt，表示短促有力的一股喷出，核心义「短而急的一下」。

sensesIntro.en: Spurt begins with liquid bursting out, then names the burst itself, and borrows the same short-and-sharp image for growth, effort, and things that happen in fits.
sensesIntro.cn: spurt 先从液体突然喷出讲起，再指那一股本身，然后把这个「短而急」的意象借给增长、用力以及断断续续发生的事情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pressed nozzle with one sharp rope of water shooting out.
core.cn: 核心意象：被挤压的喷嘴，一根水线直冲出去。

branches.en: The liquid breaking out is the basic action sense.
branches.cn: 液体冲出是基本的动作义项。

branches.en: Making the liquid shoot out is the transitive partner.
branches.cn: 使液体喷出是及物用法的对应义项。

branches.en: One counted stream is the noun sense.
branches.cn: 可数的一股是名词义项。

branches.en: A line shooting up becomes fast growth and a fast finishing effort.
branches.cn: 冲上去的那条线变成了猛增与冲刺的劲头。

branches.en: Bursts that come and stop make the phrase in spurts natural.
branches.cn: 一阵一停的特点让 in spurts 这说法很自然。

intro.en: Spurt is a native English and Germanic word; its small family is built with the regular ed and ing endings and with phrases such as growth spurt.
intro.cn: spurt 是英语和日耳曼语的本族词；它的小词族依靠常规的 -ed 与 -ing 变化，以及 growth spurt 这类词组扩展。

latinIntro.en: Spurt has no Latin origin; it belongs with German spritzen and Dutch spruiten, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: spurt 没有拉丁语来源，它与德语 spritzen、荷兰语 spruiten 同源，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Spurten is the early recorded form.
items.exampleCN: spurten 是较早的有记录形式。

items.meaning: to burst out in a short stream
items.example: Water spurted from the pipe.
items.exampleCN: 水从管道里喷了出来。

items.example: A spurt of steam hit the ceiling.
items.exampleCN: 一股蒸汽冲到了天花板。

items.example: The fountain spurts every hour.
items.exampleCN: 喷泉每小时喷一次。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: Oil spurted across the floor.
items.exampleCN: 油喷了一地。

items.example: The spurting pipe needs a new washer.
items.exampleCN: 这根正在喷水的管子需要换新垫圈。

items.example: Teenagers often have a growth spurt.
items.exampleCN: 青少年常有身高的猛长期。

items.example: The work got done in spurts.
items.exampleCN: 这活儿是一阵一阵干完的。

items.example: Air spurted out of the tyre.
items.exampleCN: 气从轮胎里喷了出来。

items.example: She saved energy for a final spurt.
items.exampleCN: 她留着力气做最后冲刺。

items.meaning: coming out in a short stream
items.example: The spurting tap soaked the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 正在喷水的水龙头把布打湿了。

definition_zh: 争吵；口角；为小事争吵；（人名）斯奎博
definition_en: to argue noisily with someone about something small, or a noisy argument of this kind
core_image: 两个人为一点小事拉扯推搡、吵吵嚷嚷
scene: 两个孩子在客厅里为争夺遥控器吵了起来，妈妈只好过来调停。Now finish your homework, or the two of you will start squabbling over the television again.
sceneCN: 这里 squabble 是动词「吵嘴」（第 1 个义项：为了小事吵吵嚷嚷）；句意：先做完作业，否则你们两个又要为看电视吵起来了。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，指「爱争吵的人」
由动词加 -ing 构成，指「没完没了的吵嘴」
由名词加 -some 构成，形容「爱为小事争吵的」（较罕见）

senses.title: To argue about something small
senses.definition: to argue noisily with someone, usually about something not serious
senses.definitionCN: 与人吵吵嚷嚷地争执，通常是为了不严重的小事
senses.example: The brothers squabbled over the last slice of cake.
senses.exampleCN: 兄弟俩为最后一块蛋糕吵了起来。
senses.why: Probably from a Scandinavian source meaning to shout; the loud, petty argument is the original image.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「大声嚷嚷」的词；吵吵嚷嚷的小争执就是它的原始意象。

senses.title: A noisy petty argument
senses.definition: a noisy argument about something unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 因为不重要的事而发生的吵闹争执
senses.example: Their squabble lasted about five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的口角持续了大约五分钟。
senses.why: The noun names the same event: a short, noisy little quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 名词指同一件事本身：一场短暂而吵闹的小口角。

senses.title: To argue with someone at length
senses.definition: to keep arguing with someone in an annoying way over time
senses.definitionCN: 长时间反复地与某人争执，令人厌烦
senses.example: The committee squabbled for weeks without deciding anything.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会吵了好几个星期，什么也没决定下来。
senses.why: The shout image stretches to long, repeated disputes, often with a feeling of annoyance.
senses.whyCN: 「嚷嚷」的画面被延展到长期反复的争端，并且往往带有不耐烦的情绪。

senses.title: An ongoing disagreement
senses.definition: a continuing dispute between people or groups about details
senses.definitionCN: 人或团体之间就细节持续存在的分歧
senses.example: The squabble between the two neighbours was never settled.
senses.exampleCN: 两位邻居之间的争执始终没能解决。
senses.why: When a petty quarrel is left unresolved, it becomes a lasting dispute.
senses.whyCN: 当小口角迟迟得不到解决时，它就会变成持久的纠纷。

intro.en: Squabble is of Scandinavian origin; a connection with the old word for a small person is suggested by some, but the origin is not certain.
intro.cn: squabble 来自斯堪的纳维亚语，或与表示「矮胖、小个子」的古词有关，但来源不确定。

items.en: Scandinavian languages provide many English words of loud speech and mild conflict.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚语为英语提供了许多与高声说话、轻微冲突有关的词。

items.en: A vowel change from skvabbe, a small, stumpy person, is one suggested source; the origin is not certain.
items.cn: 一种假说认为它由 skvabbe（矮胖矮小的人）变化而来；来源不确定。

items.en: The verb squabble is recorded in English by around 1600, meaning to quarrel noisily.
items.cn: 动词 squabble 约在十七世纪初见于英语，意为「吵闹地争执」。

items.en: The noun squabble follows the verb and names a petty quarrel.
items.cn: 名词 squabble 随后出现，指琐碎的小争吵。

items.en: Modern English keeps both verb and noun, usually for minor disputes.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词和名词两种用法，通常指小争执。

note.en: Squabble sits among quarrelsome words such as quarrel and bicker, and looks like other English words beginning with squ-.
note.cn: squabble 与 quarrel、bicker 等「争吵」词相邻，外形上又和以「squ-」开头的英语词相近。

entries.definition: very dirty and unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏的；与 squabble 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a short high-pitched sound
entries.definitionCN: 尖细的吱吱声；与 squabble 只是首字母串相同，词源不同

entries.definition: to crush something flat
entries.definitionCN: 压扁；挤压；与 squabble 只是首字母串相同，词源不同

entries.definition: to have an angry argument
entries.definitionCN: 争吵；吵架

entries.definition: to argue about unimportant things
entries.definitionCN: 为小事拌嘴

entries.definition: a disagreement or argument
entries.definitionCN: 争端；争论

normalIntro.en: Squabble is a small, noisy quarrel: short in meaning, sharp in sound.
normalIntro.cn: squabble 是小而吵闹的争执：意思不大，声音却很刺耳。

normal.en: Squabble often goes with over or about for the thing argued about.
normal.cn: squabble 常与 over 或 about 连用，后接争吵的对象。

normal.en: The words squabble over and squabble about are the most common patterns.
normal.cn: squabble over 与 squabble about 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The word comes through Scandinavian influence, not from Latin.
normal.cn: 这个词经斯堪的纳维亚语的影响进入英语，并非来自拉丁语。

normal.en: Compare quarrel: a squabble is smaller, noisier and usually shorter.
normal.cn: 对比 quarrel：squabble 更琐碎、更吵闹，通常也更短暂。

normal.en: Squabbling is often used for children or for petty committees.
normal.cn: squabbling 常用来形容孩子，或为琐事争执的委员会。

abstract.en: Picture two children pulling at one toy and shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子拉扯同一个玩具并大喊大叫。

abstract.en: The sharp start of the word echoes the sharpness of the voices.
abstract.cn: 词首尖锐的音正好呼应争吵的声音。

abstract.en: Imagine a short storm that blows over in minutes.
abstract.cn: 想象一场几分钟就过去的小风暴。

examples.en: My parents squabble about money almost every weekend.
examples.cn: 我父母几乎每个周末都为钱拌嘴。

examples.en: The squabble between the two shops was soon forgotten.
examples.cn: 那两家商店之间的口角很快就被人忘了。

examples.en: Stop squabbling, dinner is ready.
examples.cn: 别吵了，晚饭好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死烤布」——吵得脸红脖子粗，像把情绪放在火上烤；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自古北欧语支（斯堪的纳维亚语）的 skvabbe（矮胖矮小之物、闲话），一说是由 skvabbe 演变而来；与表示「大声嚷嚷」的语音意象相关，具体词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Squabble starts as a noisy little argument about something small and stretches to longer disputes and unresolved quarrels.
sensesIntro.cn: squabble 起初指为小事吵吵嚷嚷的争执，后来扩展到长时间的争论与无法了结的纠纷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people pulling at one thing and shouting over it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人拉扯同一件东西，并为此大声嚷嚷。

branches.en: The verb names the noisy act of arguing over something small.
branches.cn: 动词指为小事吵闹争执的行为。

branches.en: The noun names the brief quarrel itself.
branches.cn: 名词指这场短暂的口角本身。

branches.en: Repeated noise turns the small quarrel into a long contest of words.
branches.cn: 反复的吵闹把小口角拖成旷日持久的争辩。

branches.en: An unsettled quarrel hardens into a lasting dispute.
branches.cn: 没有解决的口角固化成持久的纠纷。

branches.en: Noun and verb describe the same petty, noisy event.
branches.cn: 名词和动词描述的是同一场琐碎而嘈杂的事件。

intro.en: Squabble has little internal structure in English; its family is small, built with -er, -ing and -some.
intro.cn: squabble 在英语中几乎看不出内部结构；它的词族很小，由 -er、-ing、-some 构成。

latinIntro.en: Squabble is not Latin; it is probably Scandinavian, so the Latin family is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: squabble 不是拉丁词，一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语，因此拉丁同族词留空。

items.meaning: to argue noisily about small things
items.example: Squabble keeps the old shouting image.
items.exampleCN: squabble 保留了「大声嚷嚷」的旧意象。

items.example: The suffix -er forms squabbler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 squabbler。

items.example: A squabbler argues about everything.
items.exampleCN: squabbler 什么事都要争。

items.meaning: an action or an ongoing process
items.example: The suffix -ing forms squabbling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 squabbling。

items.example: Squabbling filled the house.
items.exampleCN: 屋子里充满了争吵声。

items.example: The suffix -some forms squabblesome.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -some 构成 squabblesome。

items.example: The squabblesome cousins drove us mad.
items.exampleCN: 好争吵的表兄弟把我们烦透了。

items.example: Squabbling voices rose from the kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 厨房里传来争吵声。

definition_zh: 压扁；挤压；压碎；击败；镇压；壁球；南瓜类瓜果；果汁饮料
definition_en: to press something with force so that it becomes flat or crushed, or a soft fruit such as a marrow, or a racket game
core_image: 手掌用力压下去，一颗柔软的东西瞬间被压扁
scene: 厨娘准备做汤，把煮软的蔬菜用勺子按成泥。The cook squashed the soft vegetables into a thick soup.
sceneCN: 这里 squash 是动词「压扁、压成泥」（第 1 个义项：用力把某物压扁或压碎）；句意：厨娘把煮软的蔬菜压成浓汤。

pos.zh: 压扁；挤压；压碎；击败；镇压
壁球；南瓜类瓜果；软饮料

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -y 构成，义为「软烂的；一压就变形的」
squashy 的比较级，义为「更软烂的」
squashy 的最高级，义为「最软烂的」

senses.title: To press something flat or crushed
senses.definition: to press something with force so that it becomes flat, soft or broken
senses.definitionCN: 用力压某物，使其变扁、变软或破碎
senses.example: All my clothes had been squashed in the suitcase.
senses.exampleCN: 我的衣服在箱子里全被压扁了。
senses.why: The oldest verb sense, probably from French esquasser, is the hand pressing down until something goes flat.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的动词义一般认为来自法语 esquasser，就是一只手往下按，把东西压平。

senses.title: To push into a small space
senses.definition: to force yourself or something into a space that is too small
senses.definitionCN: 把自己或某物硬塞进过小的空间
senses.example: Five people squashed into the back of a tiny car.
senses.exampleCN: 五个人挤进一辆小汽车的后座。
senses.why: If pressing makes things flatter, pressing many things together makes them fit a small space.
senses.whyCN: 既然按压能把东西压扁，把许多东西按在一起自然就能塞进狭小的空间。

senses.title: To defeat or silence
senses.definition: to beat an opponent, or to stop an argument or protest by force
senses.definitionCN: 战胜对手，或强行制止争论与抗议
senses.example: The mayor squashed the protest before it began.
senses.exampleCN: 市长在抗议开始前就把它压了下去。
senses.why: A flattened opponent is like a squashed object, so beating and silencing copy the same press.
senses.whyCN: 被压扁的对手就像被压扁的物体，所以「击败」和「压制」都沿用了同一个按压动作。

senses.title: A game played in a walled court
senses.definition: a racket game played in a walled court with a small rubber ball
senses.definitionCN: 在围墙球场内用小橡胶球和球拍进行的运动
senses.example: She plays squash twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周打两次壁球。
senses.why: The game is named for the soft rubber ball that squashes against the wall.
senses.whyCN: 这项运动得名于撞墙时会压扁的软橡胶球。

senses.title: A gourd fruit eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: a large, soft fruit of the gourd family, eaten as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 葫芦科的大型软质果实，当蔬菜食用
senses.example: The soup is made with squash and onions.
senses.exampleCN: 这道汤是用南瓜和洋葱做的。
senses.why: The food sense is borrowed from the Narragansett word for a green vegetable, not from the verb.
senses.whyCN: 食物义借自纳拉甘西特语中「青食蔬菜」一词，与动词无关。

senses.title: An orange drink made from fruit
senses.definition: a drink made by squeezing fruit, especially orange
senses.definitionCN: 压榨水果（尤指橙子）制成的饮料
senses.example: He ordered a glass of orange squash.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯橙汁饮料。
senses.why: The drink sense grows from squeezing juice out of fruit, a mild version of the same press.
senses.whyCN: 饮料义来自从水果中挤出果汁，是同一个按压动作的轻量版。

intro.en: Squash comes from the Narragansett word askutasquash, which the English settlers shortened.
intro.cn: squash 来自北美原住民纳拉甘西特语词 askutasquash，英国移民把它截短使用。

items.en: Askutasquash means an uncooked or green vegetable eaten in that way.
items.cn: askutasquash 指的是生吃或青食的蔬菜。

items.en: English colonists shorten askutasquash to squash for a gourd eaten as a vegetable.
items.cn: 十七世纪三十年代，英国移民把 askutasquash 截短为 squash，指当菜吃的瓜类。

items.en: A separate verb squash, meaning to crush, is recorded around 1560, of uncertain origin.
items.cn: 另有一个表示「压碎」的动词 squash，约在十六世纪中叶见于文献，来源不确定。

items.en: The verb later shifts to mean to squeeze into space and to put an end to something.
items.cn: 该动词后来又引申为「挤进空间」和「终止某事」。

items.en: The drink sense comes from squash, to squeeze out juice, and squash the game gains its name in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 饮料义来自「挤出汁」的动词 squash，球类运动则在十九世纪获得这个名字。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for food, drink, sport and for crushing in general.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指食物、饮料、运动以及一般的压碎动作。

note.en: Squash looks like other squ- words and sits beside near meanings such as crush and squeeze.
note.cn: squash 外形上和以 squ- 开头的词相近，意义上则与 crush、squeeze 等比邻。

entries.definition: a short high-pitched sound
entries.definitionCN: 尖细的吱吱声；与 squash 只是首字母串相同，词源不同

entries.definition: to argue about small things
entries.definitionCN: 为小事争吵；与 squash 只是首字母串相同，词源不同

entries.definition: a long high-pitched cry
entries.definitionCN: 长而尖的叫声；与 squash 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to press something until it breaks
entries.definitionCN: 压碎；压坏

entries.definition: to press something from both sides
entries.definitionCN: 挤压；捏

entries.definition: to make something flat
entries.definitionCN: 使变平

normalIntro.en: Squash is a hand pressing down hard: food, space, opponents and even arguments all get flattened.
normalIntro.cn: squash 就是一只手用力往下按：食物、空间、对手，甚至争论，都会被压扁。

normal.en: Squash is both a verb and a noun, so squashes is the third person and the plural.
normal.cn: squash 既是动词又是名词，因此 squashes 既是三单也是复数。

normal.en: The food sense was borrowed from the Narragansett word askutasquash.
normal.cn: 食物的义项借自纳拉甘西特语词 askutasquash。

normal.en: The verb sense of squeezing into space grows from pressing.
normal.cn: 「挤进空间」的动词义由「压」延伸而来。

normal.en: Compare crush and squeeze: crush usually breaks, squeeze presses two sides.
normal.cn: 对比 crush 与 squeeze：crush 往往压坏，squeeze 是从两侧挤压。

normal.en: Play squash means the racket game, eaten squash means the vegetable.
normal.cn: play squash 是打壁球，eaten squash 则是当菜吃的瓜。

abstract.en: Picture a tomato under a heavy heel.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗西红柿被沉沉的脚跟压扁。

abstract.en: Imagine five people on a sofa built for three.
abstract.cn: 想象五个人挤在一张只够三个人的沙发上。

abstract.en: Think of an argument stamped out like a small fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论像小火苗一样被一下踩灭。

examples.en: The suitcase was so full that my shirt got squashed.
examples.cn: 箱子太满了，我的衬衫被压得皱巴巴的。

examples.en: We squashed four people into the back of the taxi.
examples.cn: 我们四个人挤进了出租车后座。

examples.en: Could I have an orange squash, please.
examples.cn: 请给我一杯橙汁饮料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死夸洗」——使劲「压」着东西夸它洗得干净，其实是把污渍压出来；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 名词义来自北美纳拉甘西特语 askutasquash（生吃或青食的瓜）；动词义（压碎）约十六世纪出现，词源不确定，一般认为与古法语 esquasser（压碎）有关。

sensesIntro.en: Squash begins with the hand pressing something flat, then widens to squeezing into space, to beating an opponent, and to food, drink and sport.
sensesIntro.cn: squash 从用手把东西压扁开始，扩展到挤进空间、击败对手，再延伸到食物、饮料和运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm pressing down and something soft going flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌按下去，柔软的东西被压扁。

branches.en: The literal sense is pressing something flat or crushed.
branches.cn: 字面义是把某物压扁或压碎。

branches.en: Pressing becomes squeezing when things are pushed into a small space.
branches.cn: 当东西被塞进小空间时，「压」就变成了「挤」。

branches.en: A person or argument can be flattened like a soft object.
branches.cn: 人或争辩也能像软物一样被压平。

branches.en: Food, drink and the court game all come from the noun, while the drink echoes the squeezing of juice.
branches.cn: 食物、饮料与球场运动都源自名词，其中饮料义呼应「挤出汁」的动作。

branches.en: Both pressing flat and squeezing into space share the same hand pressure.
branches.cn: 压扁与挤进空间共享同一种手部压力。

intro.en: Squash is mostly a whole word, but English builds squashy, squashes and the name of the game around it.
intro.cn: squash 基本是一个整体词，但英语围绕它造出了 squashy、squashes 以及球类名称。

latinIntro.en: Squash is not Latin: the food sense is Algonquian and the verb sense is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: squash 不是拉丁词：食物义来自阿尔冈昆语系，动词义来源不确定。

items.example: Squash names the pressing action.
items.exampleCN: squash 指压的动作。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms squashed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 squashed。

items.example: The squashed box would not open.
items.exampleCN: 被压扁的盒子打不开了。

items.example: The suffix -y forms squashy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 squashy。

items.example: The squashy sofa swallowed us.
items.exampleCN: 软乎乎的沙发把我们陷了进去。

items.example: The suffix -ier makes squashier.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ier 构成 squashier。

items.example: This pillow is squashier than that one.
items.exampleCN: 这个枕头比那个更软。

items.example: The squashiest fruit went off first.
items.exampleCN: 最软的那个果子最先坏了。

items.meaning: a court game and a gourd
items.example: Squash also names a game and a fruit.
items.exampleCN: squash 还可以指运动和水果。

definition_zh: 吱吱声；尖叫声；发出吱吱声；勉强通过；险胜
definition_en: a short, high-pitched sound, or the act of making such a sound, or to just manage to succeed
core_image: 一扇生锈的门轴轻轻一转，发出又细又短的尖响
scene: 深夜，有人悄悄推开那扇旧木门，门轴立刻发出一声细细的尖叫。The old door gave a faint squeak as she pushed it open.
sceneCN: 这里 squeak 是名词「尖锐的短音」（第 1 个义项：又短又尖的声音）；句意：她推门时，那扇旧门发出了一声细细的尖叫。

pos.zh: 发出吱吱声；勉强通过；告密

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -y 构成，义为「吱吱作响的；声音尖细的」
由 squeaky 加 -ly 构成，义为「以尖细的声音」
由 squeaky 加 -ness 构成，义为「尖细刺耳的性质」

senses.title: A short high-pitched sound
senses.definition: a very short, high sound, like the noise of a mouse or a rusty hinge
senses.definitionCN: 像老鼠或生锈铰链发出的又短又尖的声音
senses.example: We heard a squeak from inside the cupboard.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见柜子里传出吱吱声。
senses.why: The word imitates the sound itself, so the sound is the original and first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿的就是声音本身，所以「声音」是最原始、最直接的义项。

senses.title: To make a high sound
senses.definition: to make a short, high sound, or to speak in such a voice
senses.definitionCN: 发出短而尖的声音，或用这种嗓音说话
senses.example: The rocking chair squeaked as she sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐下时摇椅吱吱作响。
senses.why: Once the noun names a sound, the verb naturally names the act of producing it.
senses.whyCN: 名词既已命名了这种声音，动词自然就表示发出这种声音的动作。

senses.title: To just succeed
senses.definition: to succeed by only a very small amount
senses.definitionCN: 以极小的差距获得成功
senses.example: Our team squeaked through to the final.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队勉强挤进了决赛。
senses.why: A tight fit makes a squeak, so passing by a narrow margin is described as squeaking through.
senses.whyCN: 挤进窄缝时东西会吱吱作响，所以只以极小差距过关就说成 squeak through。

senses.title: To give away a secret
senses.definition: to tell someone in authority about another person, especially to avoid trouble
senses.definitionCN: 向有权者揭发他人，尤其为了自己脱身
senses.example: He squeaked on his friends to save himself.
senses.exampleCN: 为了自保，他把朋友供了出去。
senses.why: A mouse squeaks when it is caught, so telling on others to escape trouble uses the same cry.
senses.whyCN: 老鼠被抓到时会吱吱叫，为了脱身而告发别人便借用了同一种叫声。

intro.en: Squeak is an echoic word, imitating the small, high sound it names; its origin is not recorded as a Latin root.
intro.cn: squeak 是拟声词，模仿它所表示的那种细小而尖锐的声音；它并非来自拉丁词根。

items.en: The form is probably a changed imitation of a simple sound word such as squeak, sounding thin and small.
items.cn: 这一形式可能是对简单拟声词的改造，听起来又细又小。

items.en: Forms such as squaken and squeaken appear in Middle English for a shrill cry.
items.cn: 中古英语中有 squaken、squeaken 等形式，指尖锐的叫声。

items.en: The verb squeak, to give a sharp cry, is recorded in English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 动词 squeak（发出尖锐叫声）在十四世纪见于英语文献。

items.en: A fresh sense develops from the sound of a mouse: to tell on someone.
items.cn: 从老鼠的叫声又发展出一个新义：告发他人。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of barely passing, as if slipping through a narrow gap.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了「勉强通过」之义，好像从窄缝里挤了过去。

note.en: Squeak looks like other squ- words and joins the family of sharp little sounds such as creak and squeal.
note.cn: squeak 外形和以 squ- 开头的词相近，意义上则见于 creak、squeal 这类细碎尖声的词群。

entries.definition: to press something flat
entries.definitionCN: 压扁；与 squeak 只是首字母串相同，词源不同

entries.definition: making a high short sound
entries.definitionCN: 吱吱作响的；squeak 加 -y 构成的形容词

entries.definition: to press from both sides
entries.definitionCN: 挤压；与 squeak 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a long harsh sound of something rubbing
entries.definitionCN: 嘎吱声

entries.definition: a long, high, loud cry
entries.definitionCN: 尖叫声

entries.definition: a loud high unpleasant cry
entries.definitionCN: 刺耳尖叫

normalIntro.en: Squeak is a sound you can almost hear: short, sharp and thin, like a mouse or a gate.
normalIntro.cn: squeak 是一个几乎能听见的声音：短、尖、细，像老鼠或一扇门。

normal.en: Squeak is echoic, built to imitate a small high sound.
normal.cn: squeak 是拟声词，生来就模仿细小尖锐的声音。

normal.en: Squeak through is the favourite pattern for barely passing a test.
normal.cn: squeak through 是「勉强通过考试」最常用的搭配。

normal.en: Compare squeal: squeal is longer and louder, squeak is shorter and thinner.
normal.cn: 对比 squeal：squeal 更长更响，squeak 更短更细。

normal.en: The adjective squeaky keeps the same image, as in a squeaky door.
normal.cn: 形容词 squeaky 延续同一意象，如吱吱作响的门。

normal.en: Squeak by and squeak through both suggest squeezing past an obstacle.
normal.cn: squeak by 与 squeak through 都暗示从障碍边挤过去。

abstract.en: Picture a mouse sliding out of a hole with a tiny squeak.
abstract.cn: 想象一只老鼠一边钻出洞口，一边发出细小的吱响。

abstract.en: Imagine a rusty gate opened just wide enough for you.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇生锈的门只开到你刚好能过的宽度。

abstract.en: Think of a student passing by one mark and breathing out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个学生只多考了一分，才松了口气。

examples.en: The mouse made a tiny squeak in the corner.
examples.cn: 老鼠在角落里发出一声细小的吱叫。

examples.en: Her chair squeaked every time she moved.
examples.cn: 她一动，椅子就吱吱作响。

examples.en: He squeaked through the exam with the lowest pass mark.
examples.cn: 他以最低的及格分勉强通过了考试。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死叽克」——刻意把牙关咬紧，挤出「叽」的一声；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拟声词，模仿细小尖锐的声音；中古英语已有 squeaken 等形式，与 squeal、squeak 一类的拟声词同出一类，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: Squeak goes from a small high sound to the act of making it, and then to slipping through by a narrow margin.
sensesIntro.cn: squeak 从细小尖锐的声音，到发出这种声音的动作，再到「从窄缝里勉强挤过」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rusty hinge giving one thin, short cry.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇生锈的铰链发出一声又细又短的尖叫。

branches.en: The sound itself is the first and clearest sense.
branches.cn: 声音本身是最早、最清楚的义项。

branches.en: The verb names the action of producing that sound.
branches.cn: 动词指发出这种声音的动作。

branches.en: A narrow success feels like squeaking through a gap.
branches.cn: 勉强的成功就像从窄缝里挤过去。

branches.en: A high, thin voice is also the voice of someone informing on others.
branches.cn: 又高又细的嗓音也成了告密者说话的声音。

branches.en: Noun and verb describe the same small sharp noise.
branches.cn: 名词和动词描述的是同一种细小尖锐的响声。

intro.en: Squeak is echoic, but English still builds a small family around it with -y, -ly, -ness and common phrasal verbs.
intro.cn: squeak 是拟声词，但英语仍用 -y、-ly、-ness 和常见动词短语为它构造了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Squeak has no Latin source; it imitates sound, so the Latin family is empty.
latinIntro.cn: squeak 没有拉丁语来源，它模仿声音，因此拉丁同族词留空。

items.meaning: to make a high short sound
items.example: Squeak imitates its own sound.
items.exampleCN: squeak 模仿的就是它所指的声音。

items.example: The suffix -y forms squeaky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 squeaky。

items.example: The squeaky wheel needs oil.
items.exampleCN: 吱吱响的轮子该上油了。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms squeakily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 squeakily。

items.example: The hinges turned squeakily.
items.exampleCN: 铰链转起来吱吱作响。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms squeakiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 squeakiness。

items.example: The squeakiness of the old bed kept me awake.
items.exampleCN: 旧床的吱呀声让我睡不着。

items.meaning: to pass by a very small margin
items.example: Squeak through adds the idea of a narrow gap.
items.exampleCN: squeak through 附加了窄缝的意象。

items.example: Squeak by suggests scraping past trouble.
items.exampleCN: squeak by 暗示擦着困难挤过去。

definition_zh: 喷出；喷射；挤出（液体）；喷出的一股液体；喷嘴；冲洗管；小不点（口语）
definition_en: to force a thin stream of liquid out suddenly, or the thin stream itself, or a small tube that shoots liquid
core_image: 拇指捏紧软管，一缕细水突然喷出来
scene: 婴儿把瓶子倒过来，奶嘴猛地喷出一小股牛奶，落在餐桌上。The baby tipped the bottle upside down and squirted a thin line of milk across the table.
sceneCN: 这里 squirt 是「喷出、喷射」（第 1 个义项：把小股液体猛地射出来）；句意：婴儿把瓶子倒过来，让一小股牛奶喷到了桌面上。画面是一条又细又急的水线，而不是慢慢流动。

pos.zh: 喷出的一股液体；喷嘴；冲洗管；小不点（口语）

derivatives.zh: 喷东西的人或物；喷射器（squirt + -er，表示施动者）
爱喷水的；容易喷溅的（squirt + -y，口语构词）

senses.title: To force liquid out in a thin stream
senses.definition: to force liquid out suddenly in a thin, fast stream, usually by pressing or squeezing a container
senses.definitionCN: 通过挤压容器等方式，把液体猛地以细而快的流束射出来
senses.example: She squirted sun cream onto her palms.
senses.exampleCN: 她往手心里挤出了防晒霜。
senses.why: The word starts with the skw cluster that English also uses for wet, splashing things such as squeeze and squelch, so the opening sound itself still carries the pressing, spitting motion.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以类似挤水声的起始音节开头，英语里挤、挤压一类表示湿漉漉或挤压动作的词也多用这种发音，所以读音本身就带着「一挤就射出来」的动感。

senses.title: The liquid that is squirted
senses.definition: a small amount of liquid that shoots out in a stream
senses.definitionCN: 一次喷出的一小股液体
senses.example: Add a squirt of lemon to the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 往鱼上挤一点柠檬汁。
senses.why: In English, the act a verb describes often turns into the noun for its result, so the spray itself becomes a squirt, as with a splash or a spray.
senses.whyCN: 英语里动词描述的动作可以变成指动作结果的名词，比如溅出的水或喷雾，所以喷出来那一股液体本身也叫 squirt，正如 a splash 就是溅起的水。

senses.title: A small jet or nozzle
senses.definition: a small nozzle, tube, or jet from which liquid is squirted for washing or squirting
senses.definitionCN: 用来喷水清洗或注水的小嘴、细管或出水口
senses.example: The hot water came from a small squirt beside the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 热水是从水槽边的一个小喷嘴流出来的。
senses.why: Once the action is fixed as spraying, the thing built for spraying takes the same name by metonymy, just as a spray denotes both the spray and the sprayer.
senses.whyCN: 动作固定成「喷射」之后，专门用来喷的器具也就借用了同一个词，正如 spray 既指喷出的雾也指喷壶，这是以工具代动作的换喻。

senses.title: A small or insignificant person
senses.definition: a small, young, or unimportant person, used in informal or slightly contemptuous speech
senses.definitionCN: 小而年幼或不重要的人，多用于口语，带点调侃或不屑
senses.example: Just a squirt like you should not tell me my job.
senses.exampleCN: 像你这样的小不点还没资格教我做事。
senses.why: The core image of a thin, brief jet gave the word a sense of something small and of little weight, and that shrank onto people, turning a thin stream into a little person.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一股又细又短的液流，这种「小、不起眼」的感觉被用到人身上，细水线就缩成了小人物。

senses.title: To cause someone to be sprayed
senses.definition: to spray liquid over someone or something, often playfully
senses.definitionCN: 把液体朝某人或某物喷去，常带有玩耍性质
senses.example: The boys squirted each other with the garden hose.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们用花园水管互相喷水。
senses.why: From directing a jet at a target, English naturally extends the verb to its object, so squirting someone means making them the person who gets sprayed.
senses.whyCN: 从小股液流射向某个目标，英语顺手把动词延伸到接受动作的人身上，所以 squirting someone 就是把人当成被喷的对象。

intro.en: Squirt is a word of uncertain origin that first appeared in late Middle English in the fifteenth century, and it has stayed a lively everyday word for spraying and spouting.
intro.cn: squirt 词源不确定，十五世纪末的中古英语里就已出现，之后一直作为表示「喷射、喷出」的常用口语词沿用至今。

items.en: Squirt is first recorded in English in the fifteenth century as a verb meaning to shoot out liquid.
items.cn: squirt 在十五世纪的中古英语里首次被记录，作动词表示液体喷射而出。

items.en: Its origin is uncertain: no Latin or French source is firmly established, so the word is treated as an English formation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：并没有可靠的拉丁语或法语来源，因此通常把它看作英语本土形成的词。

items.en: The initial skw- sound echoes squeeze and squelch, comparing with the squelching motion of pressing wet things.
items.cn: 词首的读音与英语挤压水声的联想一致，可以对照挤压湿东西时挤出声响的一类动词。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries squirt names both a thin jet of water and a small instrument for squirting, such as a syringe.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，squirt 既指一股细水流，也指喷水的小器具，例如注射用的喷管。

items.en: Modern English adds informal uses: a squirt can be a small person, and squirt gun and squirt bottle are everyday compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语加上了口语用法：squirt 可以指小个子的人，还组成了水枪、挤压瓶一类日常复合词。

note.en: Squirt sits among the sound-driven spray words squeeze and squelch, and next to the wider spray family of spurt, spray, and jet.
note.cn: squirt 属于挤压、喷溅这类拟声连想的词，和 spurt、spray、jet 等表示「喷」的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: to press something firmly, often to get liquid out of it
entries.definitionCN: 用力挤压，常指把液体挤出来；与 squirt 只是读音和动作联想相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make a wet, sucking sound when walked on or pressed
entries.definitionCN: 踩在湿处时发出吱嘎的水声；与 squirt 只是读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a toy gun that shoots water
entries.definitionCN: 喷洒水的玩具水枪（squirt 加 gun 构成的复合词）

entries.definition: to gush out suddenly in a short, strong burst
entries.definitionCN: 突然喷出、涌出一阵，常指一阵有力的短喷

entries.definition: to scatter liquid in fine drops over something
entries.definitionCN: 把液体散成细雾喷到某物上

entries.definition: a strong stream of liquid or gas that shoots out
entries.definitionCN: 喷射而出的强劲液流或气流

normalIntro.en: Squirt is a squeezing word: a container is pressed, and a thin line of liquid shoots out.
normalIntro.cn: squirt 是「一挤就出」的词：容器被捏紧，一缕细水猛地射出来。

normal.en: Squirt out means liquid shoots out, as when a cut tube starts leaking.
normal.cn: 「squirt out」表示液体喷出来，就像管子裂了开始往外射。

normal.en: A squirt gun is a toy that shoots water, so the gun is named after the spray.
normal.cn: 水枪就是喷水的玩具，玩具的名称直接用了「喷射」这个词。

normal.en: A squirt of lemon means one quick squeeze of juice.
normal.cn: 「一小挤柠檬」就是迅速挤出的一点柠檬汁。

normal.en: The common two forms are squirting and squirted, with the t doubled only before -ing.
normal.cn: 常见变形是 squirting 与 squirted，t 只在加 -ing 时双写。

normal.en: Compare spurt: spurt is a strong sudden burst, squirt is a thin stream pushed out by pressure.
normal.cn: 对比 spurt：spurt 强调突然的猛烈喷涌，squirt 强调受压挤出的细流。

abstract.en: Picture a ketchup bottle: you press the neck and a red line lands on the chip.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶番茄酱：捏住瓶身，一条红线落在薯条上。

abstract.en: Think of a small boy with a water pistol, shooting a thin jet at a friend.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小男孩拿水枪，朝朋友射出一道细水线。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny nozzle beside the tap, spitting hot water for washing.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头旁边一个小喷嘴，喷出热水供冲洗用。

examples.en: He squirted a little toothpaste onto his brush.
examples.cn: 他往牙刷上挤了一点牙膏。

examples.en: A thin jet of water squirted from the leaking pipe.
examples.cn: 一股细水从漏水的管道里喷了出来。

examples.en: The cleaner added a squirt of detergent to the bucket.
examples.cn: 清洁工往桶里挤了一点洗涤剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死阔特」——瓶子一挤，水「嗖」地窜出去，又快又细；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 词源不确定：一般认为无可靠的拉丁语或法语来源，属于英语本土形成的拟声倾向词，词首读音与「挤压、喷溅」的联想一致；现代义项由「细流喷射」引申出「喷嘴」「小不点」等概念。

sensesIntro.en: Squirt first means to force out a thin stream, then the small amount and the nozzle it comes from, then the playful act of spraying someone, and finally a tiny person.
sensesIntro.cn: squirt 先用来说「喷出细流」，再指喷出的那一小股以及喷水的嘴，然后指朝人喷水的动作，最后延伸为口语里的「小人物」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thumb pressing a tube so a thin stream shoots out.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指捏住软管，一缕细流射出去。

branches.en: The action of forcing liquid out is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 把液体挤射出来是基本义项。

branches.en: The narrow amount of liquid named after the action is the result sense.
branches.cn: 以动作命名的那一小股液体是结果义项。

branches.en: A small jet for washing is the tool sense.
branches.cn: 用于冲洗的小喷嘴是工具义项。

branches.en: The thin, brief stream shrank onto a small person in speech.
branches.cn: 又细又短的液流在口语里缩成了「小人物」。

branches.en: Aiming the jet at someone gives the object sense.
branches.cn: 把水流指向某人，就得到「朝人喷水」的宾语义项。

intro.en: Squirt is a native English word with few affixes; it grows mainly through compounds such as squirt gun and through the noun-forming -er in squirter.
intro.cn: squirt 是英语本土词，构词很少；它主要通过水枪这类复合词以及构成施动名词的词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Squirt has no established Latin or French source, so it is not a Latin affix word; the Latin connection here is only by comparison.
latinIntro.cn: squirt 没有可靠的拉丁语或法语来源，不属于拉丁词缀词；这里的拉丁语对比仅供联想。

items.meaning: to force out a thin stream
items.example: Squirt is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: squirt 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.meaning: a thin jet or the spray it gives
items.example: The same shape names the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 同一词形既指动作也指结果。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.example: The suffix -er forms squirter.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 squirter。

items.meaning: a person or thing that squirts
items.example: Squirter adds an agent to the verb.
items.exampleCN: squirter 在动词上加了施动者含义。

items.example: The suffix -y forms squirty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 squirty。

items.example: Squirty describes something that sprays easily.
items.exampleCN: squirty 描述容易喷溅的东西。

items.example: Squirt gun joins the spray word with gun.
items.exampleCN: 水枪把「喷射」与「枪」组合在一起。

items.meaning: a bottle that shoots liquid when squeezed
items.example: Squirt bottle names a squeezing container.
items.exampleCN: 挤压瓶是常用来喷挤液体的容器。

definition_zh: 刺；戳；捅；刺伤；刺痛的突然一击；一阵（疼痛）；尝试（口语）
definition_en: to push a sharp point or knife into something, or a sudden sharp pain, or an attempt at something
core_image: 一把尖刀直直扎进皮肉，又短又快
scene: 试做蛋糕那阵子，她把刀扎进蛋糕中心，拔出来看有没有熟。She stabbed a knife into the middle of the cake and pulled it out to see whether it was done.
sceneCN: 这里 stab 是「刺入、扎进」（第 1 个义项：用尖利的东西快速扎下去）；句意：她用刀扎进蛋糕中心再拔出来，看看烤熟了没有。画面是一个短促、向下的尖利动作。

pos.zh: 刺；戳；刺痛；一阵（疼痛）；尝试（口语）

derivatives.zh: 持刀伤人事件；像刀刺一样的（stab + -ing）
持刀伤人者（stab + -er，表示施动的人）
如刀刺般地；尖锐地（stabbing + -ly，较少用）

senses.title: To push a knife or sharp point into something
senses.definition: to push a pointed weapon or sharp object quickly and forcefully into someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用尖利的武器或器物快速用力扎进身体或物体
senses.example: Two men stabbed him near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 两名男子在车站附近刺伤了他。
senses.why: Stab is first a strike: the word arrived in late Middle English as the name of a thrusting blow, and the verb still shows that short, hard, forward push.
senses.whyCN: stab 最初是一种击打：它在中古英语晚期进入英语，指一次向前戳出的打击，所以动词至今仍带着那种短促、用力向前顶的感觉。

senses.title: A wound or a stabbing attack
senses.definition: a wound made by a sharp point, or the crime of wounding someone with a knife
senses.definitionCN: 由尖器造成的伤口，或持刀伤人的行为与案件
senses.example: He died from a single stab wound to the chest.
senses.exampleCN: 他因胸口一处刀伤而死亡。
senses.why: The verb is concrete and violent, so its noun names the concrete result on the body: the one wound that one thrust makes.
senses.whyCN: 动词具体而暴力，它的名词便自然指向身体上看得见的结果：一次扎刺留下的那一道伤。

senses.title: A sudden sharp feeling
senses.definition: a sudden short feeling of pain or a strong emotion, like a quick jab inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂的一下疼痛或强烈情绪，好像身体内部被扎了一下
senses.example: I felt a stab of guilt when I saw her face.
senses.exampleCN: 看到她的脸时，我感到一阵内疚。
senses.why: The image of one quick thrust maps onto feeling: a pain that comes and goes in a single sharp jab is felt as one stab rather than a steady ache.
senses.whyCN: 一次快速扎刺的画面被映射到感受上：像一下子扎过来又立刻收走的痛，人们就称之为一阵刺痛，而不是隐隐作痛。

senses.title: An attempt at something
senses.definition: an attempt to do something, especially in the phrases take a stab or have a stab at
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的尝试，常见于「试一下」这类口语说法
senses.example: Let me take a stab at answering that.
senses.exampleCN: 让我试着回答一下这个问题。
senses.why: English plays with the idea of a thrust: a shot at a target is a try, so take a stab means push once at the problem and see whether you hit.
senses.whyCN: 英语借用了「扎一下」的意象：朝目标扎一次就是一次尝试，所以「试着扎一下」引申为「试一试，看能不能扎中」。

senses.title: A sharp movement into something
senses.definition: to push a finger or a sharp tool quickly into or through a surface
senses.definitionCN: 用手指或尖利工具快速地戳进或穿过某个表面
senses.example: She stabbed the button and the lift doors shut.
senses.exampleCN: 她猛地按了一下按钮，电梯门就关上了。
senses.why: Once the core act is a quick jab, any short, hard pushing motion, even at a button, can borrow the same verb and the same impatient energy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦核心动作被理解为快速一戳，任何短促用力的推送，哪怕只是按按钮，也能借用这个动词和这种不耐烦的劲头。

intro.en: Stab appeared in late Middle English, and its deeper origin is uncertain: the best-supported idea links it to the same Germanic family as stick, stitch, and the German word for a thorn.
intro.cn: stab 在中古英语晚期出现，更早的来源不确定；较有支撑的推测认为它与 stick（戳）、stitch（缝）以及德语中表示「刺、尖刺」的词同属日耳曼语族一支。

items.en: A Germanic root is compared, and modern German has the related forms stechen for to prick and Stachel for a sting or thorn.
items.cn: 可以对照日耳曼语族的词根：德语中与「刺、扎」相关的动词和表示「刺、尖刺」的名词同属这一组。

items.en: Old English already had stingan for to pierce or prick, the ancestor of modern sting.
items.cn: 古英语已有表示「刺、扎」的动词 stingan，它是现代 sting 的前身。

items.en: Stab is first recorded in the fifteenth century; dictionaries mark its earlier origin as uncertain.
items.cn: stab 在十五世纪才首次被记录，词典对它的更早来源标注为不确定。

items.en: The noun stab is recorded from around the sixteenth century, and the figurative take a stab at appears later.
items.cn: 名词 stab 大约从十六世纪起有记录，「试一试」的比喻用法出现得更晚。

items.en: Modern English keeps the short, sharp sense in a stab of pain and in the everyday phrase stab in the back.
items.cn: 现代英语在「一阵刺痛」和「背后捅刀」这类说法里保留了那种短促、尖锐的感觉。

note.en: Stab belongs to the poking and piercing group of sting, stick, pierce, and prick, and its nearest everyday neighbours are the injury nouns wound and cut.
note.cn: stab 与 sting、stick、pierce、prick 同属「扎、刺」的动作词群，与它最近的日常近义词还有表示伤口的 wound 与 cut。

entries.definition: the past simple and past participle of stab
entries.definitionCN: stab 的过去式和过去分词，拼写时词尾 t 以外双写 b 再依次加词尾

entries.definition: an attack in which someone is stabbed, or a sudden sharp pain
entries.definitionCN: 持刀伤人的事件，也可形容像刀刺一样的剧痛

entries.definition: a person who stabs someone
entries.definitionCN: 持刀刺人的人

entries.definition: to hurt with a small sharp point, as an insect does
entries.definitionCN: 用细小尖锐的部位刺人，如昆虫蜇人；与 stab 同属日耳曼语族「刺」的词群

entries.definition: to push a pointed object into or through something
entries.definitionCN: 用尖物刺入或穿透；与 stab 同属「扎、戳」的动作词群

entries.definition: to make a hole in something with a sharp point
entries.definitionCN: 用尖器穿透、在物体上扎出孔洞

normalIntro.en: Stab is a short, hard word for a short, hard act: one forward push with a sharp point.
normalIntro.cn: stab 这个字又短又硬，正好对应又短又狠的动作：拿着尖器用力向前一顶。

normal.en: Stab someone in the back means to betray someone behind their back.
normal.cn: 「在背后捅一刀」就是当面不说什么，背后背叛别人。

normal.en: Take a stab at it means try it, even if the first attempt misses.
normal.cn: 「试一下」就是先试一次，哪怕第一下没扎中。

normal.en: A stab of pain is one quick hit of pain, not a long ache.
normal.cn: 一阵刺痛就是很快的一下痛，而不是长时间的隐痛。

normal.en: Remember the past form stabbed: the b is doubled before the endings -ed and -ing.
normal.cn: 记住过去式 stabbed：加 -ed 和 -ing 时词尾的 b 要双写。

normal.en: Compare stick and sting: stick is the action, sting is what insects and thorns do, and stab points to a blade.
normal.cn: 对比 stick 与 sting：stick 泛指戳的动作，sting 多指昆虫或刺的扎，stab 则特指刀刃的刺。

abstract.en: Picture a knife held straight down, then driven into the tabletop in one motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把刀竖直握好，一下子扎进桌面。

abstract.en: Think of a single drop of blood on a torn sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象破袖子上沾着一滴血。

abstract.en: Imagine a needle of feeling: one quick jab of sorrow inside the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一根感情的细针，在胸口快速扎了一下就收走。

examples.en: The victim was stabbed in the shoulder.
examples.cn: 受害者肩膀被刺伤了。

examples.en: She felt a stab of disappointment when the results came out.
examples.cn: 结果出来时，她感到一阵失望。

examples.en: Why not take a stab at writing the report yourself?
examples.cn: 为什么不自己试着写这份报告呢？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死大夫」——一刀扎下去，就得去等大夫（医生）了；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 词源不确定：一般认为与日耳曼语族表示「扎、刺」的词根同源，可对照德语中表示「刺」的动词与表示「尖刺」的名词，以及古英语中表示「刺」的动词 stingan（现代 sting 的前身）；stab 在十五世纪的中古英语里才被记录。

sensesIntro.en: Stab begins with the physical jab of a blade, then the wound it leaves, then the sharpness of a feeling, an attempt, and finally any quick hard push.
sensesIntro.cn: stab 从刀刃的实际一扎出发，接着指留下的伤口，再引申为感觉那一下尖锐的刺，然后是尝试，最后扩展到任何短促用力的戳按。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade driven straight into the flesh in one quick thrust.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃一下子直直扎进皮肉。

branches.en: The physical thrust with a blade is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 用刀刃实际扎刺是基本义项。

branches.en: The result on the body is the concrete injury sense.
branches.cn: 身体上留下的结果是具体的刀伤义项。

branches.en: A single sharp jab is borrowed for pain and emotion.
branches.cn: 一次快速的尖锐动作被借用来表示疼痛与情绪。

branches.en: One thrust at a problem becomes one attempt in speech.
branches.cn: 对着问题扎一下，在口语里就成了一次尝试。

branches.en: Any short hard push, even at a button, keeps the same energy.
branches.cn: 任何短促用力的戳按，哪怕是按按钮，都保留了同一股劲。

intro.en: Stab takes few affixes; it forms its family with the endings that mark verbs and agents, as in stabbing and stabber, and with compounds such as stab wound.
intro.cn: stab 能加的词缀不多，主要是构成动词形式和施动名词的词尾，以及后面加名词组成的短语，比如刀伤。

latinIntro.en: Stab is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin entries; the Latin words listed for comparison are only near-synonyms, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: stab 属日耳曼语族而非拉丁语系，因此没有拉丁同源词；这里的拉丁语词仅供意义对比，并非词源同族。

items.meaning: to pierce with a sharp point
items.example: Stab is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: stab 是这个词族的基础词。

items.example: The noun names the blow and its result.
items.exampleCN: 名词同时指扎刺的动作与造成的伤。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed gives stabbed, with b doubled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 stabbed，其中 b 需要双写。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives stabbing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 stabbing。

items.example: The suffix -er forms stabber.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 stabber。

items.example: Stabber names the person who does the act.
items.exampleCN: stabber 指做出这个动作的人。

items.example: Stabbing also warns of a knife attack in the news.
items.exampleCN: stabbing 在新闻里也常指持刀伤人的案件。

items.meaning: a wound made by a knife
items.example: Stab wound joins the verb with the noun for injury.
items.exampleCN: 刀伤是把动词与伤的名词组合起来。

latinEntries.example: Latin punctus lies behind English puncture, not behind stab.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 punctus 是英语 puncture 的来源，并非 stab 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Latin pungere gives English pungent and puncture.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pungere 派生出英语中的 pungent 与 puncture。

latinEntries.example: Latin punctum is a useful contrast, not an ancestor.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 punctum 是很好的对照词，但不是 stab 的祖先。

definition_zh: 使稳定；使稳固；稳定下来；稳住（局面、物价、病人状态）；（技术）使处于稳定/平衡状态
definition_en: to make something firm, steady, or unlikely to change or fall, or to become steady
core_image: 摇晃的桌子被塞进一块木片，桌面终于不再晃
scene: 汇率剧烈波动的最后一个月，各国央行联手出手，试图让市场平静下来。The central bank stepped in to stabilise the currency after weeks of sharp swings.
sceneCN: 这里 stabilise 是「使稳定、稳定下来」（第 2 个义项：把波动的局面稳下来）；句意：在汇率剧烈震荡数周之后，央行出手干预，试图让货币稳定下来。画面是一个摇摇晃晃的东西被稳稳托住。

pos.zh: 使稳定；使稳固；稳定下来

derivatives.zh: 稳定；稳定化处理（stabilise + -ation，构成名词）
稳定器；稳定剂（stabilise + -er，表示起作用的器具或物质）
稳定性；稳定（拉丁语 stabilitas，同源名词）
稳定的；稳固的；马厩（同根形容词，词源另有「马厩」一义）

senses.title: To make something firm and steady
senses.definition: to make a physical object firm so that it cannot move, rock, or fall
senses.definitionCN: 使实物变得牢固，不再晃动、摇晃或倒下
senses.example: Workers stabilised the wall with steel supports.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们用钢支架把墙体固定好。
senses.why: Latin stabilis means standing firm, from the verb stare, to stand: to stabilise something is literally to make it stand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 stabilis 意为「站立稳固」，源自动词 stare（站立）；所以「使稳定」字面上就是「让某物站住」。

senses.title: To make a situation calm and steady
senses.definition: to make prices, a market, a country, or a situation calm and steady after a period of change or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 使价格、市场、国家或局势在变动或动荡之后平静、稳定下来
senses.example: The government brought in new rules to stabilise food prices.
senses.exampleCN: 政府出台了新规定，以稳定食品价格。
senses.why: The image of a thing that keeps on its feet moved from walls to markets: prices and public moods also sway, so we stabilise them too.
senses.whyCN: 「站得稳」的意象从墙扩展到市场上：物价和民心也会摇摆，所以也可以让它们稳定下来。

senses.title: To become steady
senses.definition: to become steady and no longer get worse, used of patients, conditions, or numbers
senses.definitionCN: 变得平稳、不再恶化，多用于病人状况或数据
senses.example: Her condition has stabilised since the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她的病情已经稳定下来。
senses.why: A verb that means to make steady also serves as a plain statement of being steady, so a patient stabilises once the rocking of the illness slows.
senses.whyCN: 表示「使……稳」的动词也可以直接描述「变稳」本身，所以病人一旦病情不再起伏，就叫「稳定下来」。

senses.title: To keep something in a fixed state
senses.titleCN: （技术）使稳定；使保持稳定状态
senses.definition: to keep a material, image, concrete, camera, or chemical process in a fixed and balanced state
senses.definitionCN: 使材料、影像、混凝土、相机或化学过程保持在固定、平衡的状态
senses.example: The camera has a motor that stabilises the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机有一个电机来稳定镜头。
senses.why: Technical uses take the same core idea, keeping an object or process from wobbling, and make it an engineering goal, so concrete is stabilised and so is a photo.
senses.whyCN: 技术领域沿用同一核心：让物件或过程不再晃，并把它当成工程目标，于是混凝土要「做稳定处理」，照片也要「防抖」。

senses.title: To prevent something from getting worse
senses.definition: to stop a bad trend or illness from getting worse and hold it level
senses.definitionCN: 让恶化的趋势或病情停止加坏，保持在原来程度
senses.example: Emergency staff stabilised him before the ambulance left.
senses.exampleCN: 急救人员在救护车出发前先让他的状况稳住，不再恶化。
senses.why: If the goal of stabilising is that nothing falls, then holding a falling condition level is the same act applied to health and economic trends.
senses.whyCN: 如果「使稳定」的目标是不让东西倒下，那么把正在下滑的状况稳稳托住，就是同一动作用于健康和经济走势。

intro.en: Stabilise is a learned English borrowing from Latin: it goes back to stabilis, standing firm, which is built on stare, to stand, through the French spelling stabiliser.
intro.cn: stabilise 是从拉丁语借来的学术用词：它源自 stabilis（站立稳固），而 stabilis 又由 stare（站立）构成，途中又受到法语 stabiliser 拼写的影响。

items.en: A reconstructed root shared by Latin stare, English stand, and Greek histanai means to stand.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare、英语 stand 与希腊语中表示「站立」的动词共享重构的原始印欧语词根。

items.en: Latin stare means to stand, and its derived adjective stabilis means firm, standing still, and not rocking.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，由它得来的形容词 stabilis 意为牢固的、站着不动的、不摇晃的。

items.en: The related verb stabilire means to make firm, and the noun stabilitas means firmness or stability.
items.cn: 同族动词 stabilire 意为使牢固，名词 stabilitas 意为稳固、不变。

items.en: French forms stabiliser and stabilisation develop from Latin sources in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十八世纪由拉丁来源发展出 stabiliser 与 stabilisation。

items.en: English forms stabilise in the nineteenth century, and the American spelling stabilize settles beside it later.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪形成 stabilise，后来的美式拼写 stabilize 与之并存。

note.en: Stabilise is the verb built on the Latin adjective for standing firm, so it is closely tied to stable and stability, and it shares a meaning field with balance and steady.
note.cn: stabilise 是由拉丁语中表示「站得稳」的形容词衍生出的动词，与 stable、stability 关系最近，语义上与 balance、steady 等词相邻。

entries.definition: firm and not likely to change or fall
entries.definitionCN: 稳定的；稳固的（与目标词同根）

entries.definition: the state of being firm and steady
entries.definitionCN: 稳定性；稳定（拉丁语 stabilitas，同源名词）

entries.definition: the act of making something steady
entries.definitionCN: 稳定化；使稳定的过程（stabilise + -ation）

entries.definition: to make something firm or steady
entries.definitionCN: 使牢固、使稳住；与 stable 同含「站住」的义感

entries.definition: to keep something in an even position so it does not fall
entries.definitionCN: 使保持平衡、不倒下

entries.definition: to fix something firmly so it cannot move
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定住，使其不能移动

normalIntro.en: Stabilise carries stand inside it: the word makes a thing stand so firmly that nothing can rock it.
normalIntro.cn: stabilise 里藏着「站」：它让某样东西站稳到谁也摇不动。

normal.en: The base is stable, and the ending -ise turns the adjective into a verb meaning to make stable.
normal.cn: 词干是 stable，词尾把形容词变成动词，意思就是「使……变得稳定」。

normal.en: The noun stabilisation is in the family, as in the long stabilisation of prices.
normal.cn: 同族名词 stabilisation 表示「稳定、稳定化过程」，比如物价的长期稳定。

normal.en: The -iser ending names the thing that does the steadying, as in a voltage stabiliser.
normal.cn: 以 -iser 结尾的词指起稳定作用的东西，比如稳压器。

normal.en: British writes stabilise and American writes stabilize, and both take the same endings in -ed and -ing.
normal.cn: 英式拼写是 stabilise，美式拼写是 stabilize，两者加 -ed、-ing 的词尾写法相同。

normal.en: In medical English to stabilise a patient means to keep the vital signs from getting worse.
normal.cn: 在医学英语里，让病人「稳定下来」指让各项生命体征不再恶化。

abstract.en: Picture a wobbly table with a folded card pushed under one leg.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摇晃的桌子，在一条腿下塞进一张折起来的卡片。

abstract.en: Imagine a steep market chart that finally flattens into a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条陡升陡降的行情曲线，最后变成一条平直的线。

abstract.en: Think of a patient whose breathing slows and becomes even after panic.
abstract.cn: 想象一个病人从慌乱中平静下来，呼吸变得均匀。

examples.en: The new dam will help stabilise water levels in the valley.
examples.cn: 新水坝将有助于稳定山谷里的水位。

examples.en: Investors waited for the share price to stabilise.
examples.cn: 投资者在等股价稳定下来。

examples.en: Medics stabilised the injured climber before moving him.
examples.cn: 医护人员先稳住受伤登山者的状况，再把他转运走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死得平稳」——让人「稳稳当当不倒下」，就是使稳定；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）→ stabilis（站得稳的、牢固的）→ stabilire（使牢固）→ 法语 stabiliser → 英语 stabilise（美式拼写 stabilize），核心义「让某物稳稳站住、不再动摇」。

sensesIntro.en: Stabilise starts with making a physical object stand firm, then extends to prices and situations, to patients becoming steady, to technical processes held fixed, and to stopping a downward trend.
sensesIntro.cn: stabilise 先指把实物固定得站得稳，再扩展到物价、局势，接着指病情稳定下来、技术过程保持固定，最后指遏制恶化的趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot planted firm, so the thing above it stops rocking.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚下踩稳，上面的东西不再晃。

branches.en: Making a physical object firm is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 把实物固定牢固是字面义项。

branches.en: Prices and situations are swayed and steadied in the same way.
branches.cn: 物价与局势同样会摇摆，也可以用同一方式稳住。

branches.en: A patient who becomes steady gives the plain state sense.
branches.cn: 病人状况变稳，给出的是状态义项。

branches.en: Engineering keeps cameras and concrete in a fixed state.
branches.cn: 工程领域让相机、混凝土等保持固定状态。

branches.en: Holding a falling trend level is the preventive sense.
branches.cn: 托住正在下滑的趋势，是预防性的义项。

intro.en: Stabilise is built on the Latin root meaning to stand, plus the verb-forming ending -ise, and it sits in a large family of stable, stability, and stabiliser words.
intro.cn: stabilise 由表示「站立」的拉丁词根加上构成动词的词尾 -ise 组成，并与 stable、stability、stabiliser 一起构成一个大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilis means standing firm and comes from stare, to stand; English uses these forms through Latin and French, which is why the word takes the Latin -ise ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stabilis 意为站立稳固，来自 stare（站立）；英语经由拉丁语和法语引入这些词形，所以才采用拉丁式的动词词尾。

items.example: Latin stare is where the standing picture begins.
items.exampleCN: 「站立」的画面从拉丁语 stare 开始。

items.example: Stabilis adds firmness to the idea of standing.
items.exampleCN: stabilis 在「站立」之上加了「牢固」。

items.example: Stabilire makes the firmness into an action.
items.exampleCN: stabilire 把「牢固」变成动作。

items.example: Stabilitas gives the English noun stability.
items.exampleCN: stabilitas 是英语名词 stability 的来源。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns the adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: Stabilise is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: stabilise 是这个词族的动词。

items.meaning: a device or substance that steadies something
items.example: Stabiliser names the thing that keeps balance, as on a bike.
items.exampleCN: stabiliser 指保持平衡的器具，比如自行车上的辅助轮。

items.meaning: the process of being made steady
items.example: Stabilisation names the process of becoming steady.
items.exampleCN: stabilisation 指使稳定的过程。

items.example: The prefix un- gives the opposite unstable.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀 un- 构成反义的不稳定。

definition_zh: 舞台工作人员；后台杂工
definition_en: a person who works behind or beside the stage, moving scenery, props, and equipment during a performance
core_image: 舞台侧幕后面，穿黑衣的人影在黑暗里推着布景前进
scene: 音乐剧换幕的间隙，侧台一片黑暗，工作人员在黑幕里飞快地搬走旧布景。The stagehands moved the heavy scenery into the wings in complete darkness.
sceneCN: 这里 stagehand 是「舞台工作人员」（第 1 个义项：在舞台后方操作布景与道具的人）；句意：舞台工作人员在完全黑暗的侧台把沉重的布景搬走。

pos.zh: 舞台工作人员；后台杂工

collocations.zh: 舞台工作人员移动布景

collocations.phrase: hire a stagehand for the show
collocations.zh: 为演出雇一名后台工人

derivatives.zh: stagehand 加词尾 -ing 构成，口语指「舞台搬景工作」
stage 加 management 构成的复合词，指「舞台管理」，与舞台工作人员分工相邻

senses.title: A person who moves scenery and props
senses.definition: a crew member who moves scenery, furniture, and props on and off the stage during a play
senses.definitionCN: 在戏剧演出中把布景、家具和道具搬上搬下舞台的剧组成员
senses.example: Two stagehands carried the painted tree off between scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 两场之间，两名舞台工作人员把那棵彩绘树搬了下去。
senses.why: The compound joins stage with hand, an old word for a worker, so the literal meaning is a person who lends a hand on the stage.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 stage（舞台）与 hand（旧时指干活的人）合在一起，字面就是「在舞台上搭把手的人」，所以先指搬景的道具员。

senses.title: An unskilled backstage worker
senses.definition: a general backstage worker who does heavy or simple jobs such as carrying, cleaning, and setting up
senses.definitionCN: 在后台干重活或简单工作的杂工，如搬运、清扫和布置场地
senses.example: During the tour she worked as a stagehand, unpacking and washing the costumes.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演期间她当后台杂工，负责拆包和清洗戏服。
senses.why: Because hand points to labour rather than skill, the word also covers anyone doing plain backstage work, not only scenery movers.
senses.whyCN: 因为 hand 强调的是出力干活而非技艺，所以这个词也泛指在后台做普通杂活的人，并不只限于搬布景的人。

senses.title: A hidden helper behind a show
senses.definition: a person who works quietly behind the scenes so that another person or event looks good
senses.definitionCN: 在幕后默默出力、让别人或某个活动看起来出色的人
senses.example: In the debate club he acted as a stagehand, preparing every fact the speakers used.
senses.exampleCN: 在辩论社里他充当幕后帮手，准备演讲者用到的每一个事实。
senses.why: An invisible crew makes the visible performance possible, so the word widens from backstage crew to anyone who props up a public show.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的剧组成员让看得见的演出成为可能，于是这个词从后台工作人员扩展到任何撑起台前风光的人。

intro.en: Stagehand is an English compound of stage and hand, where hand was once a plain word for a hired worker.
intro.cn: stagehand 是 stage 与 hand 组成的英语复合词，其中 hand 旧时泛指受雇干活的人。

items.en: Latin statio means a standing place, from stare, to stand.
items.cn: 拉丁语 statio 意为站立之处，源于 stare（站）。

items.en: Old French estage means a floor or a dwelling, from the Latin root.
items.cn: 古法语 estage 意为楼层或住所，来自上述拉丁词根。

items.en: Stage enters English as a raised platform or floor.
items.cn: stage 进入英语，指抬高的台子或地板。

items.en: Hand comes to mean a hired worker, and stage means the theatre platform.
items.cn: hand 逐渐指受雇的工人，stage 则指剧场的演出台。

items.en: Stagehand, first recorded in the nineteenth century, names the crew who shift scenery.
items.cn: stagehand 最早见于十九世纪，指搬动布景的剧组成员。

note.en: Stagehand sits inside the theatre crew family and next to general words for workers and helpers.
note.cn: stagehand 属于剧场后台工作人员这一家族，同时与泛指工人和助手的词相邻。

entries.definition: the raised platform where actors perform
entries.definitionCN: 演员表演的演出台

entries.definition: a hired worker, especially one doing practical jobs
entries.definitionCN: 受雇的工人，尤指干体力活的人

entries.definition: in or to the area behind the stage
entries.definitionCN: 在后台，指舞台后面的区域

entries.definition: a group of people working together on a production
entries.definitionCN: 为同一个演出一起工作的一群人

entries.definition: a person who operates lights or sound for a show
entries.definitionCN: 为演出操作灯光或音响的技术人员

entries.definition: a person who helps actors change costumes
entries.definitionCN: 帮演员更换戏服的人

normalIntro.en: Stagehand is a compound you can simply take apart: a hand on the stage.
normalIntro.cn: stagehand 是一个可以拆开理解的复合词：在舞台上搭把手的人。

normal.en: Stage plus hand gives a worker who lends a hand at the stage.
normal.cn: stage 加 hand 就是在舞台上搭把手的工作人员。

normal.en: Hand alone can still mean a hired worker, as in farm hand.
normal.cn: hand 本身可指受雇的工人，如 farm hand 就是农场雇工。

normal.en: Backstage is the area where stagehands wait and work.
normal.cn: backstage 指后台，是舞台工作人员等待和干活的地方。

normal.en: In a paper copy of a theatre programme, the crew are listed as stage staff.
normal.cn: 在剧场节目单的纸本里，这类工作人员常被列作「舞台组」。

normal.en: Compare technician: a stagehand mostly lifts and carries, a technician operates equipment.
normal.cn: 对比 technician：舞台工作人员多负责搬运，技术人员操作设备。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of black gloves gripping the edge of a painted flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一副黑手套抓住一块彩绘布景板的边沿。

abstract.en: Hear the soft rumble of wheels as scenery glides into the wings.
abstract.cn: 听布景滑轮滚进侧台时那阵低低的隆隆声。

abstract.en: See a figure in black slip away just before the curtain rises.
abstract.cn: 想象大幕拉开前，一个黑衣身影悄悄退场。

examples.en: A stagehand in black pulled the curtain closed without being seen.
examples.cn: 一名身穿黑衣的舞台工作人员在没人察觉的情况下拉上了幕布。

examples.en: The show was short of money, so the actors helped the stagehands set the furniture.
examples.cn: 演出经费不足，于是演员们帮着舞台工作人员摆家具。

examples.en: Every night the stagehand checked that the trap door was firmly locked.
examples.cn: 每天晚上，这位舞台工作人员都要检查活动地板门是否锁牢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯泰季汉德」——舞台边那个「汉德」出手帮忙；这只是读音联想，真正的构词是 stage 加 hand。

root: stage（舞台，源于拉丁语 stare「站」经古法语 estage 而来）+ hand（旧时指受雇干活的人）→ stagehand，核心义「在舞台上出力干活的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Stagehand starts as the crew member who moves scenery, then broadens to any plain backstage worker, and at last to a hidden helper behind any show.
sensesIntro.cn: stagehand 先指搬布景的剧组成员，再泛指后台杂工，最后引申为任何演出的幕后帮手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in black pushing scenery through the wings in darkness.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中一个黑衣身影把布景推进侧台。

branches.en: The literal sense covers the crew who shift scenery and props.
branches.cn: 字面义指搬动布景和道具的剧组成员。

branches.en: The broad sense covers any plain backstage labour.
branches.cn: 宽义指后台任何普通的体力杂活。

branches.en: The figurative sense names the invisible helper behind success.
branches.cn: 比喻义指成功背后看不见的帮手。

branches.en: Moving scenery and washing costumes are both the work of hired hands at the stage.
branches.cn: 搬布景与洗戏服都属于在舞台上干活的人的份内事。

branches.en: Both the backstage worker and the hidden helper serve others without being seen.
branches.cn: 后台杂工与幕后帮手都在不被看见的情况下为他人服务。

intro.en: Stagehand is a two-part English compound, built from stage and the general worker word hand.
intro.cn: stagehand 是一个由两部分组成的英语复合词，前一部分是 stage，后一部分是泛指工人的 hand。

latinIntro.en: Only the first part reaches Latin: stage goes back through Old French to Latin statio, a standing place.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半部分可追溯到拉丁语：stage 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 statio（站立之处）。

items.example: Stare is the base of the Latin word for a standing place.
items.exampleCN: stare 是拉丁语「站立之处」一词的基础。

items.example: Statio later gives the idea of a fixed platform.
items.exampleCN: statio 后来引申出固定台子的意思。

items.example: Estage carries the Latin root into French.
items.exampleCN: estage 把拉丁词根带进法语。

items.meaning: a raised platform, a theatre platform
items.example: Stage is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: stage 是复合词的前一半。

items.example: Hand as a worker appears in farm hand and deckhand.
items.exampleCN: hand 指工人的用法见于农场雇工与水手等词。

items.example: Backstage marks where the crew work.
items.exampleCN: backstage 标明工作人员干活的位置。

items.meaning: a sailor who does ordinary work on deck
items.example: Deckhand shows the same worker pattern with deck.
items.exampleCN: deckhand 用 deck 展示了同样的构词模式。

items.example: Stage fright contrasts with the calm work of the stagehand.
items.exampleCN: 怯场与舞台工作人员的沉着忙碌形成对照。

items.meaning: an instruction in a script about movement
items.example: Stage direction is another stage compound.
items.exampleCN: stage direction 是另一个含 stage 的复合词。

definition_zh: 停滞；不流动；不发展；变得呆滞
definition_en: to stop flowing or moving, and so to stop developing or making progress
core_image: 一片池水被水草堵住，表面浮着绿膜，不再流动
scene: 雨停之后，后院的池塘没有出口，水面浮起一层绿膜，蚊虫在闷热的空气里打转。The pond behind the house stagnated until its surface turned green.
sceneCN: 这里 stagnate 是「停滞、不流动」（第 1 个义项：水不流动或某事物停止发展）；句意：屋后的池塘渐渐停滞不流，直到水面变成绿色。

collocations.zh: 在无前途的工作中原地踏步

derivatives.zh: 动词加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ant 构成，义为「停滞的；不流动的」
动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「停滞；不流动」
由形容词 stagnant 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「停滞状态」

senses.title: To stand still like blocked water
senses.definition: to stop flowing or moving, as still water does when nothing stirs it
senses.definitionCN: 停止流动或运动，就像没有东西搅动的一潭死水
senses.example: Without rain, the water in the ditch began to stagnate.
senses.exampleCN: 没有雨，沟里的水开始停滞发臭。
senses.why: The Latin verb stagnare means to flood or form a pool, so the core picture is water that has stopped moving.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 stagnare 意为「积水成池」，核心画面就是水停止流动，因此第一义项是物理上的停滞。

senses.title: To stop growing or progressing
senses.definition: of an economy, business, or field, to fail to grow or make progress
senses.definitionCN: 用于经济、企业或领域，指不再增长或没有进展
senses.example: Sales stagnated for three quarters before the new model appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 新款出现之前，销量连续三个季度停滞不长。
senses.why: Still water neither rises nor moves, and so the image transfers to any activity that has lost its current.
senses.whyCN: 死水既不上涨也不流动，于是这个意象被搬到任何失去动力的活动上，指经济和企业不再增长。

senses.title: Of a person, to lose drive
senses.definition: of a person or mind, to become dull and stop developing because nothing new comes in
senses.definitionCN: 用于人或心智，指因输入新鲜事物而变得迟钝、停止成长
senses.example: He stagnated in the same office for years, doing work he had long outgrown.
senses.exampleCN: 他在同一个办公室原地踏步多年，做着自己早已不再有挑战的工作。
senses.why: A mind left without new ideas is like a pool without a stream, so the word comes to describe personal dullness.
senses.whyCN: 心智没有新想法进入，就像没有活水的池子；因此这个词也用来形容个人变得迟钝、不再成长。

intro.en: Stagnate comes from Latin stagnare, to form a pool of standing water, from stagnum, a pool.
intro.cn: stagnate 来自拉丁语 stagnare（积成死水），源于 stagnum（池塘、水洼）。

items.en: Stagnum means a pool of still water.
items.cn: stagnum 意为静止的池水。

items.en: Stagnare means to overflow or to form a pool.
items.cn: stagnare 意为溢出或积成一潭水。

items.en: Stagnatus, the past participle, is used of water that has stopped running.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语使用过去分词 stagnatus，形容停止流动的水。

items.en: Stagnate enters English to describe water and then any state that fails to move.
items.cn: stagnate 于十七世纪进入英语，先形容水，继而形容任何不再推进的状态。

items.en: Economists and writers now use it for markets, wages, and people who have stopped growing.
items.cn: 现代英语中，经济学家和作家用它描述市场、工资以及不再成长的人。

note.en: Stagnate is the verb of still water, closely tied to stagnant and stagnation, and near words for lack of progress.
note.cn: stagnate 是「死水」家族里的动词，与 stagnant、stagnation 紧密相连，也与表示「不前进」的词相邻。

entries.definition: not flowing or moving
entries.definitionCN: 不流动的

entries.definition: the state of not flowing or growing
entries.definitionCN: 停滞；不发展的状态

entries.definition: the quality of being stagnant
entries.definitionCN: 停滞状态

entries.definition: to stop suddenly and be unable to continue
entries.definitionCN: 突然停下，无法继续

entries.definition: to be forced to remain in a bad state and become weak
entries.definitionCN: 被迫处于不良状态而日渐衰弱

entries.definition: to reach a level and stay there without further change
entries.definitionCN: 达到某一水平后不再变化

normalIntro.en: Stagnate shares its Latin root with stagnant and stagnation, so all three keep the idea of water that stops moving.
normalIntro.cn: stagnate 与 stagnant、stagnation 共享同一个拉丁词根，三个词都保留「水停止流动」的意思。

normal.en: Stagnant is the adjective and stagnation the noun of the same root.
normal.cn: stagnant 是同根形容词，stagnation 是同根名词。

normal.en: The particle -ate marks a verb, as in activate and estimate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标志动词性质，正如 activate 与 estimate。

normal.en: Latin stagnum, a pool, keeps the image of water with no stream.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 stagnum（池塘）保留了没有活水的水面这一意象。

normal.en: An economy that stagnates shows no growth, just as a pool shows no flow.
normal.cn: 经济停滞就像池水不流：都没有增长，也没有流动。

normal.en: Compare start: to start is to set in motion, the exact opposite of standing still.
normal.cn: 对比 start：start 是让东西动起来，正好与停住不动相对。

abstract.en: Picture a puddle under a hot sun, ringed by a dark green rim.
abstract.cn: 想象烈日下一个水洼，边缘围着一圈墨绿色的浮膜。

abstract.en: See a clock on a wall whose second hand has stopped between two marks.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的钟，秒针卡在两个刻度之间停住不动。

abstract.en: Feel a runner standing at the start line, breathing hard, never beginning.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者站在起点线上大口喘气，却始终不迈出第一步。

examples.en: Left in a warm corner of the room, the fruit juice quickly stagnates.
examples.cn: 放在房间温暖的角落里，果汁很快就停滞变质了。

examples.en: Government spending has stagnated while the population keeps growing.
examples.cn: 人口不断增长，政府开支却停滞不前。

examples.en: She feared that her career would stagnate if she stayed in the same city.
examples.cn: 她担心如果留在同一座城市，自己的事业会停滞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死特格内特」——死水「格」外「内」「特」久都不流动；这只是谐音联想，真正的词源是拉丁语 stagnum（池塘）。

root: 拉丁语 stagnum（池塘、死水）→ stagnare（积水；停止流动）→ 英语 stagnate，核心义「像没有出口的死水一样停住」。

sensesIntro.en: Stagnate begins with water that stops flowing, moves to activities that stop growing, and ends with people whose minds or careers stop developing.
sensesIntro.cn: stagnate 从水停止流动说起，延伸到活动停止增长，最后指人的心智或事业不再发展。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pool closed off with no stream running through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个封闭起来、没有活水流进流出的池子。

branches.en: Water that stops flowing is the first and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 水停止流动是最先出现、也最具体的义项。

branches.en: An economy that stops growing borrows the same still-water picture.
branches.cn: 经济停止增长借用了同样的死水画面。

branches.en: A person who stops developing has a mind without a stream.
branches.cn: 停止成长的人，其心智就像没有活水的池子。

branches.en: A blocked pond and a flat market both lack any current pushing them forward.
branches.cn: 堵塞的池塘和停滞的市场都缺少推动它们向前的流动。

branches.en: In both cases the problem is the absence of something new coming in.
branches.cn: 两种情况下的问题都是没有新鲜事物流入。

intro.en: Stagnate is built on the Latin noun stagnum, a pool, with the English verb ending -ate added.
intro.cn: stagnate 以拉丁语名词 stagnum（池塘）为根，加上英语动词词尾 -ate 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin stagnum means a pool of still water, and stagnare is its verb of flooding or pooling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stagnum 意为静止的池水，stagnare 是它表示「积水、停住」的动词。

items.example: Stagnum supplies the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: stagnum 提供这一词族的词根。

items.meaning: to flood, to form a pool
items.example: Stagnare is the direct verb source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: stagnare 是英语词的直接动词来源。

items.example: The suffix -ate turns the root into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把词根变成动词。

items.example: Stagnant describes the water before the verb is used.
items.exampleCN: stagnant 先于动词用法出现，用来形容不流的水。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms stagnant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 stagnant。

items.example: Stagnation turns the verb back into a noun.
items.exampleCN: stagnation 把动词重新变回名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms stagnation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 stagnation。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -cy forms stagnancy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 构成 stagnancy。

items.meaning: of a marsh, related to wet standing water
items.example: Palustrine wetland terms describe the same still water.
items.exampleCN: 表示沼泽湿地的术语也在描述同样的静水。

latinEntries.meaning: to flood, to form a pool

definition_zh: 不锈的；不会污损的；无瑕疵的；清白无过的
definition_en: that does not rust or become stained, or, of a person, free from blame or dishonour
core_image: 一只钢制汤匙被水淋过又擦干，表面一道水痕都没留下
scene: 餐厅后厨，厨师把汤锅用清水冲净，锅壁亮得能照出灯影，放了很久也不见锈斑。The kitchen uses stainless steel pots that keep their shine for years.
sceneCN: 这里 stainless 是「不锈的」（第 1 个义项：金属不生锈、不留污痕）；句意：这家厨房使用多年仍保持光亮的「不锈钢」汤锅。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「不留污痕地；清白地」
形容词加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「不锈性；清白无瑕」
去掉否定词尾 -less 后得到的基础词，义为「污渍；留下污痕」

senses.title: Not liable to rust
senses.definition: of metal, not rusting and keeping a clean surface when wet
senses.definitionCN: 用于金属，指不锈、遇水后表面依然干净
senses.example: The railings are made of stainless steel that stays bright in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 栏杆由不锈钢制成，在雨中依然光亮。
senses.why: The -less suffix removes the stain, so the word first promises metal that leaves no rusty or dirty mark.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -less 表示「没有」，把 stain（锈迹、污痕）去掉，所以这个词首先承诺这种金属不生锈、不留脏痕。

senses.title: Leaving no mark on a surface
senses.definition: not trapping dirt or marks, so a cloth will keep it clean with little effort
senses.definitionCN: 不容易藏污纳垢，用布一擦就干净
senses.example: She bought a stainless apron for the studio because paint wipes off it easily.
senses.exampleCN: 她为画室买了一件不留污痕的围裙，颜料一擦就掉。
senses.why: Without a stain there is nothing to clean away, so the word widens from rust to any surface that resists dirt.
senses.whyCN: 没有污痕就无需费力清洗，于是这个词从「不锈」扩展到任何抗污、易擦净的表面。

senses.title: Free from blame or dishonour
senses.definition: of a person or reputation, without any mark of wrongdoing or shame
senses.definitionCN: 用于人或声誉，指没有任何过错或羞辱的印记
senses.example: He retired after forty years with a stainless record as a judge.
senses.exampleCN: 他当了四十年法官，带着清白的记录退休。
senses.why: A stain on cloth became a stain on character in older usage, so stainless means a life with no dark mark on it.
senses.whyCN: 旧时人们把布上的污渍比作品格上的污点，所以 stainless 表示人生干净、没有污点可指。

intro.en: Stainless is formed in English from stain plus the negative suffix -less.
intro.cn: stainless 是在英语内部由 stain 加上否定词尾 -less 构成的。

items.en: Old French desteindre means to take away the colour.
items.cn: 古法语 desteindre 意为「去掉颜色」。

items.en: Steinen is recorded in the fourteenth century for colouring or dyeing cloth.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现 steinen 一词，指给布料上色或染色。

items.en: By the fifteenth century stain also means a spot of dirt or shame.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，stain 也指污点或耻辱。

items.en: Stainless appears as a poetic word for something without a mark of shame.
items.cn: 十六世纪出现 stainless 一词，在诗文中指没有耻辱印记的。

items.en: With the rise of steel that resists rust, stainless steel becomes the everyday sense.
items.cn: 随着抗锈钢材的普及，stainless steel（不锈钢）成为最常见的用法。

note.en: Stainless is a negative adjective built on stain with -less, and it belongs with words for clean, pure, and unmarked.
note.cn: stainless 是由 stain 加 -less 构成的否定形容词，属于「干净、纯洁、无瑕」这一语义场。

entries.definition: a dirty mark on a surface
entries.definitionCN: 表面的污渍

entries.definition: marked with dirt or colour
entries.definitionCN: 沾污的；留下污痕的

entries.definition: completely clean, with no spots
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有污点的；一尘不染的

entries.definition: treated so that it does not rust
entries.definitionCN: 防锈的

entries.definition: perfectly clean, or without any fault
entries.definitionCN: 一尘不染的；毫无过错的

entries.definition: a record with no mistakes or bad marks
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何污点的记录

normalIntro.en: Stainless is easy once you see the two parts: stain plus the suffix -less, which means without.
normalIntro.cn: 看懂两部分就很好记：stain 加上表示「没有」的词尾 -less。

normal.en: The suffix -less means without, as in hopeless and careless.
normal.cn: 词尾 -less 表示「没有」，正如 hopeless 与 careless。

normal.en: Stainless steel is the common phrase where the word is used today.
normal.cn: stainless steel（不锈钢）是今天最常见的固定搭配。

normal.en: Stain as a noun is a dirty mark and as a verb means to leave one.
normal.cn: stain 作名词是污渍，作动词是留下污痕。

normal.en: Spotless works the same way with spots instead of stains.
normal.cn: spotless 是同样的构词法，只是用 spot（斑点）代替 stain。

normal.en: Compare stained: stained glass has colour added, which is the opposite of stainless.
normal.cn: 对比 stained：stained glass 是「彩绘玻璃」，加了颜色，正好与 stainless 相反。

abstract.en: Watch rain bounce off a steel spoon and drain away without a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象雨点打在钢汤匙上，随即滑落，不留一丝痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a white shirt that red wine cannot mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一件被红酒泼到也留不下痕迹的白衬衫。

abstract.en: See a mirror-polished plate reflecting a clean, unbruised face.
abstract.cn: 想象一块抛光镜面映出一张干净、没有伤痕的脸。

examples.en: The new kitchen is fitted with stainless steel appliances.
examples.cn: 新厨房配备的是不锈钢电器。

examples.en: Salt water damages ordinary iron but leaves stainless steel unharmed.
examples.cn: 盐水会腐蚀普通铁，却不会损害不锈钢。

examples.en: The minister left office with a stainless reputation.
examples.cn: 这位部长带着清白的声誉离任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯泰勒斯」——「斯泰勒斯」的勺子放再久也不锈；这只是谐音联想，构词其实是 stain 加 -less。

root: 英语 stain（污渍，源自中古英语 steinen，上溯古法语 desteindre「去色」）+ 否定词尾 -less（没有……的）→ stainless，核心义「不留污痕、不生锈」。

sensesIntro.en: Stainless first describes metal that does not rust, then any surface that keeps clean, and finally a character with no mark against it.
sensesIntro.cn: stainless 先形容不锈的金属，再形容不易留污的表面，最后形容没有污点的人格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steel spoon that water runs off, leaving no mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：水珠从钢汤匙上滑落，一点痕迹也不留。

branches.en: Metal that will not rust is the technical and most common sense.
branches.cn: 不生锈的金属是最技术化、最常见的义项。

branches.en: A surface that resists dirt is the everyday extension.
branches.cn: 抗污的表面是日常用法上的延伸。
