items.example: Endurance is not a cognate but a near synonym.
items.exampleCN: endurance 并非同源词，而是近义词。

definition_zh: 口吃；结巴；说话时反复卡在某个音上
definition_en: to speak with involuntary pauses and repeated sounds, so that words come out broken
core_image: 话到嘴边卡在第一个音上，越着急越挤不出来的样子
scene: 面试官提问之后，男孩想说自己姓什么，可那个辅音总在舌尖打转，他涨红了脸，好一会儿才把名字挤出来。He stammered his name and looked down at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 stammer 是「结巴着说」（第 1 个义项：因口吃而把话卡住、断断续续地说）；句意：他结结巴巴地报出自己的名字，然后低头看着桌面。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，作名词指「口吃、结巴」
加表人的后缀 -er，指「有口吃的人」
在 stammering 后加 -ly，指「结结巴巴地」

senses.title: To speak with broken, repeated sounds
senses.definition: to speak with involuntary stops and repetitions, so that a word or sound gets stuck
senses.definitionCN: 说话时不自主地停顿、重复，某个词或音卡住出不来
senses.example: He stammered a few words before falling silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他结结巴巴地说了几个字，就沉默了。
senses.why: The word is probably imitative of the stop-and-go sound of speech that catches in the throat, so the blocking itself became the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能模仿了话在喉咙里走走停停的声音，于是「卡住」这个动作本身就成了词义。

senses.title: To say something haltingly with effort
senses.definition: to force out particular words or sentences in a hesitating, broken way
senses.definitionCN: 以迟疑、断断续续的方式把某些词或句子硬说出来
senses.example: She stammered out the bad news to her parents.
senses.exampleCN: 她断断续续地把坏消息告诉了父母。
senses.why: Once the verb names broken speech, it takes a direct object and pictures someone pushing a sentence through the gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦表示断续的话语，就能带宾语，画面变成把一整句话一点点推出那道卡口。

senses.title: The speech disorder
senses.definition: the condition or habit of speaking with involuntary stops and repetitions
senses.definitionCN: 说话时不由自主停顿、重复的病症或习惯
senses.example: Her stammer became much worse when she had to read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 每当必须大声朗读时，她的口吃就严重得多。
senses.why: The same word also names the causes as a noun: what the speaker does is the stammer and the disability is a stammer too.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也作名词指那件事的成因：说话时的表现叫 stammer，它所代表的语言障碍也叫 stammer。

senses.title: A halting, hesitating manner
senses.definition: a manner of speech that hesitates and breaks under nerves or uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 因紧张或不确定而迟疑、断裂的说话方式
senses.example: He answered without a stammer, as if the question were the simplest in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答得毫不吞吐，仿佛那是世上最简单的问题。
senses.why: Since nerves cause stammering, the noun drifts toward any halting in speech, whether or not it is a medical condition.
senses.whyCN: 既然紧张会引发结巴，名词就顺势扩展到任何迟疑的话语，哪怕根本算不上病症。

senses.title: To falter in a way like speech
senses.titleCN: （比喻）磕磕绊绊；断断续续进行
senses.definition: in figurative use, of an engine, process, or start to proceed with stops and jerks
senses.definitionCN: 比喻某事物像说话卡壳一样走走停停、断断续续
senses.example: The old engine stammered for a moment before it started.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧发动机突突咔咔了几下才启动。
senses.why: The rhythm of broken speech is easy to borrow for anything that stutters into motion, so engines and starts can stammer too.
senses.whyCN: 断断续续的说话节奏极好借用，凡是磕磕绊绊启动的东西都能 stammer，比如老发动机。

intro.en: Stammer is probably an imitative Germanic word for speech that catches, with a cognate in Middle Low German and a close relative in the verbs of stumbling speech.
intro.cn: stammer 一般认为是一个模仿「卡住的话」的日耳曼语词，在中古低地德语中有同源词，并与一组表示说话磕绊的动词关系密切。

items.en: Reconstructed forms such as stam are thought to imitate the sound of blocked speech, though the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构的形式 stam 模仿了话语受阻的声音，不过具体形态存疑。

items.en: Stammern and similar forms record the word with the same imitative sense.
items.cn: 中古低地德语的 stammern 等形式记录了相同的拟声义。

items.en: Related words for stuttering appear in Old English, but the modern spelling stammer is not attested there.
items.cn: 古英语中已有表示口吃的相关词，但现代拼写 stammer 在当时尚未见于记录。

items.en: Stameren is first recorded in English, describing speech that catches.
items.cn: stameren 首次见于英语记录，描述卡住的话语。

items.en: The verb and the noun settle into the standard forms stammer and stammering.
items.cn: 动词与名词逐渐固定为标准形式 stammer 与 stammering。

note.en: Stammer is the broken-speech verb, with imitative relatives and a cluster of near synonyms for speaking with stops and halts.
note.cn: stammer 是表示「话语断裂」的动词，形近一族是拟声同源词，近义一族集中在结巴、吞吞吐吐的表达上。

entries.definition: to speak with repeated sounds or syllables
entries.definitionCN: 结结巴巴地说，发音时反复重复；与 stammer 意义极近，拼写也相近

entries.definition: the act of speaking with broken sounds
entries.definitionCN: 由 stammer 加 -ing 构成的动名词，指口吃这件事

entries.definition: a person who stammers
entries.definitionCN: 由 stammer 加 -er 构成的表人名词，指口吃的人

entries.definition: to speak or move with hesitation and losing energy
entries.definitionCN: 说话或行动迟疑、没了底气

entries.definition: to speak quietly and not clearly
entries.definitionCN: 含糊不清地小声说

entries.definition: to make a mistake or trip while speaking or walking
entries.definitionCN: 说话或行走时绊了一下、出了岔子；与 stammer 同音感相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Stammer keeps the sound of speech catching: a stop, a repeat, and then the word squeezed out.
normalIntro.cn: stammer 保留了「话语受阻」的声音：先一停、再重复，最后才把词挤出来。

normal.en: To stammer an apology is to push an apology out in broken pieces.
normal.cn: stammer an apology 就是一句道歉被断成几截挤出来。

normal.en: Add -er to stammer and you get stammerer, a person who stammers.
normal.cn: stammer 加 -er 就是 stammerer，指口吃的人。

normal.en: In British English stutter and stammer are both used, and stammer is the more formal word.
normal.cn: 英式英语里 stutter 与 stammer 都常用，相对而言 stammer 更正式。

normal.en: The noun takes the same form as the verb: a stammer, with a nervous stammer as a common phrase.
normal.cn: 名词与动词形式相同，写成 a stammer，常见搭配是 a nervous stammer。

normal.en: Compare falter: faltering loses energy, stammering catches on a sound.
normal.cn: 对比 falter：faltering 是没了底气，stammering 是卡在一个音上。

abstract.en: Picture a key that turns, sticks, turns again, and finally opens the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙转一下、卡住、再转一下，最后才把锁打开。

abstract.en: Think of a word queue jammed at the mouth, one person pushing at a time.
abstract.cn: 想想词语在嘴边排起长队，一次只能挤出一个人。

abstract.en: Imagine a tape recorder that plays each syllable twice before moving on.
abstract.cn: 想象一台录音机每个音节都要播两遍才肯往下走。

examples.en: He stammered an apology and left the room.
examples.cn: 他结结巴巴地道了歉，然后离开了房间。

examples.en: Children who stammer often need patient support at school.
examples.cn: 有口吃的孩子在学校里往往需要耐心的支持。

examples.en: Her nervous stammer made the interview harder than it needed to be.
examples.cn: 她紧张时的结巴让面试比原本难得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死抬么」——一个字卡在嘴前死活抬不出来，就是结巴；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自日耳曼语中模仿「语音受阻」的拟声词（中古低地德语 stammern 可作参照）→ 中古英语 stamer/stameren（结巴地说）→ 现代英语 stammer；词根存疑处已标注，英式拼写保留了 -er 词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Stammer grows from the broken sound of blocked speech into forced-out words, the condition itself, a halting manner, and then a metaphor for anything that stutters into motion.
sensesIntro.cn: stammer 从「受阻的语音」起步，发展为吃力挤出的言语、语言障碍本身、吞吐的说话方式，最后比喻一切磕磕绊绊启动的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words that jam at the mouth and come out in broken pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：话语卡在嘴边，一个字一个字挤出来。

branches.en: The plain verb for speaking with stops and repeats.
branches.cn: 最基本的义项，指说话停顿、重复。

branches.en: With an object, the verb pictures a sentence squeezed out.
branches.cn: 带宾语时，动词描绘一句话被挤出来。

branches.en: The noun names the disorder itself.
branches.cn: 名词形式指口吃这一障碍本身。

branches.en: Any nervous hesitation in speech is a stammer.
branches.cn: 任何紧张造成的吞吐都可叫作结巴。

branches.en: Figurative use lets engines and processes stammer too.
branches.cn: 比喻用法让发动机、进程也能「结巴」。

intro.en: Stammer is an imitative word with no Latin prefix; its English family grows through the noun, person, and adverb endings -ing, -er, and -ly.
intro.cn: stammer 是拟声词，没有拉丁前缀；它的英语词族靠 -ing、-er、-ly 这些名词、表人与副词词尾长出来。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic rather than Latin, so Latin cognates are uncertain and only generic speech words are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语而非拉丁语，可靠的拉丁同源词存疑，此处只列出与「说话」相关的通用拉丁词。

items.example: The opening stam imitates a stop in speech.
items.exampleCN: 开头的 stam 模仿了说话时的停顿。

items.example: Stammer is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: stammer 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.example: The same form serves as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一形式也可作名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms stammering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 stammering。

items.example: The suffix -er forms stammerer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 stammerer。

items.example: Stammerer adds a person to the action.
items.exampleCN: stammerer 在动作上加了一个人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms stammeringly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 stammeringly。

items.example: Stammeringly describes the manner of speech.
items.exampleCN: stammeringly 描述说话的方式。

items.example: Stutter is a near synonym, not a Latin form.
items.exampleCN: stutter 是近义词，并非拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 立场；态度；站姿，尤指体育运动中准备发力的姿势
definition_en: a way of standing, or a fixed way of thinking about an issue, showing where one stands
core_image: 双脚分开踏稳地面，整个人稳稳立在原处，半步不退
scene: 议会辩论时，记者追问首相要站在哪一边，她放下手中的稿纸，正面回答说自己始终反对这项税。When the reporter pressed the prime minister, she made her stance on the new tax clear.
sceneCN: 这里 stance 是「立场、态度」（第 2 个义项：对某问题的固定看法与站位）；句意：记者追问首相时，她明确表达了自己对新税种的立场。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，指多个立场或站姿
由 stant-（站立）词根构成，义为「坚定不移」，属同根派生
由 sub-（在下）+ stant-（站立）构成，本义「立于其下者」，引申为「物质、实质」

senses.title: A way of standing
senses.definition: the position of the feet and body when standing, especially one that braces for effort
senses.definitionCN: 站立时双脚与身体的姿势，尤指为发力而摆出的架势
senses.example: The coach showed the children how to take a wide stance before lifting the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 教练教孩子们在提沙袋前先摆开一个宽稳的站姿。
senses.why: Stance is an aphetic form of Old French estance, meaning a standing or a stay, so its first job is simply how and where the body stands.
senses.whyCN: stance 是古法语 estance（站立、停留）脱落首音后的形式，所以它最初的本职就是「身体怎样站着」。

senses.title: A position on an issue
senses.definition: a publicly held view or attitude, especially one that is firm and looked at by others
senses.definitionCN: 公开持有、态度坚定的观点或主张，常受他人关注
senses.example: The university took a firm stance against cheating in exams.
senses.exampleCN: 校方对考试作弊持坚定立场。
senses.why: People who face a dispute plant their feet and speak from where they stand, so the bodily stance became the mental one.
senses.whyCN: 面对争论，人会把脚站稳再开口，于是身体上的「站位」转成了思想上的「立场」。

senses.title: A set posture for a sport
senses.definition: the prepared position from which a sportsperson begins a movement, as in golf, boxing, or baseball
senses.definitionCN: 运动员发动动作前摆好的预备姿势，如高尔夫、拳击与棒球中的架势
senses.example: In golf the stance sets the direction of the whole swing.
senses.exampleCN: 在高尔夫里，预备架势决定了整个挥杆的方向。
senses.why: Because to stand in a stance is to arrange the body for the next move, sportswriters borrowed the word for ready positions.
senses.whyCN: 因为摆出一个 stance 就是为下一步动作布置身体，体育写作便借它来指各种预备姿势。

senses.title: A hard, opposing attitude
senses.definition: a particularly stern or defiant way of positioning oneself toward someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事表现出的格外严厉或对抗性的立场
senses.example: Neighbours adopted a hard stance towards the new nightclub.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们对这家新夜店采取了强硬的对立姿态。
senses.why: The stance images a body squared for conflict, so the abstract sense sharpens into stubborn opposition when the feet are set against someone.
senses.whyCN: 当意象变成双脚冲着对方摆开的对抗姿势，抽象立场也随之变得强硬，成为针锋相对的态度。

senses.title: A resting place or shop in old British use
senses.definition: in old British English, a standing place or roadside stop, especially a cab or coach stand
senses.definitionCN: 旧时英式英语中供人停留的地点或路边停靠点，尤指出租马车停候处
senses.example: The old cab stance by the market has long been gone.
senses.exampleCN: 集市旁那处老式的马车停靠站早已消失。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense of standing still at a spot, kept in dialect and in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是「在某处站定不动」最古老的具体义，如今只留在方言与历史叙述里。

intro.en: Stance comes from Old French estance and ultimately from Latin stare, to stand, losing its first syllable on the way into English.
intro.cn: stance 来自古法语 estance，溯源于拉丁语 stare（站立），进入英语时脱落了开头的音节。

items.en: Stare means to stand or remain, and its present participle gives the element stans.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立、停留，其现在分词给出 stans 这一成分。

items.en: The derived noun constantia, from constare, means standing firm, the ancestor of English constancy.
items.cn: 由 constare 派生的 constantia 意为坚定站立，是英语 constancy 的祖先。

items.en: Estance and its verb estancier carry the sense of a stay or standing place.
items.cn: 古法语 estance 及其动词 estancier 带有「停留、站立之处」的意思。

items.en: Estance appears in English, meaning a standing place or a stay in one spot.
items.cn: estance 在英语中出现，指站立之处或在一地的停留。

items.en: Stance separates out as its own word, first naming a standing position and later a set attitude.
items.cn: stance 分流为独立词汇，先指站立姿势，后来才指固定的态度。

items.en: Stance moves into politics, policy, and sport, from where one stands to what one stands for.
items.cn: 现代英语中 stance 进入政治、政策与体育语境，从「站在哪里」转成「站在哪一边」。

note.en: Stance sits in the Latin family of standing words and has close neighbours among words for opinion and attitude.
note.cn: stance 隶属于拉丁语「站立」词族，近义上则与表示态度、观点的词为邻。

entries.definition: the quality of staying firm and unchanging
entries.definitionCN: 坚定不移、始终如一的品质，同源于站立词根

entries.definition: a fact or condition around an event
entries.definitionCN: 围绕某事的事实或情形，同源于站立词根

entries.definition: physical matter or the essential quality of something
entries.definitionCN: 物质或事物的实质，由在下站立构成

entries.definition: an opinion, or the place where something is put
entries.definitionCN: 立场、观点，也指所在位置

entries.definition: a settled way of feeling or thinking
entries.definitionCN: 态度、看法，侧重心里的倾向

entries.definition: the way the body is held when sitting or standing
entries.definitionCN: 坐立时的体态姿态；与 stance 的站姿义相近

normalIntro.en: Stance is a standing word: first the feet, then the body, then the opinion you refuse to give up.
normalIntro.cn: stance 本质是个「站」字：先是脚，再是身体，最后是你寸步不让的观点。

normal.en: Stance shares the Latin root stare, to stand, with constant and stable.
normal.cn: stance 与 constant、stable 共享拉丁词根 stare（站立）。

normal.en: To take a stance on something is to state clearly where you stand.
normal.cn: 在某事上表明「take a stance」，就是明确交代自己站在哪一边。

normal.en: A golf swing begins with the stance, and so does a boxing round.
normal.cn: 高尔夫挥杆从 stance 开始，拳击的每一个回合也一样。

normal.en: Change your stance on a policy and others will ask why the ground beneath you moved.
normal.cn: 在政策上 change your stance，旁人就会追问你脚下的地怎么动了。

normal.en: Compare position, which can be neutral and descriptive, while stance is usually open and firm.
normal.cn: 对比 position：它可以中立描述，而 stance 往往公开而坚定。

abstract.en: Picture a golfer setting both feet before the swing starts.
abstract.cn: 想象高尔夫球手在挥杆前把双脚摆好。

abstract.en: Imagine someone in a debate who stands and does not lean.
abstract.cn: 想象辩论中的某个人一直站着，一次都不往椅背靠。

abstract.en: Think of a boxer in a guarded stance, weight low and eyes forward.
abstract.cn: 想想拳击手的防守架势：重心压低，目光向前。

examples.en: The government has changed its stance on fuel subsidies.
examples.cn: 政府改变了在燃油补贴上的立场。

examples.en: Experts questioned the minister for taking a hard stance.
examples.cn: 专家们质询部长为何采取强硬立场。

examples.en: A wide stance keeps the knees safe during the exercise.
examples.cn: 做这个动作时，宽稳的站姿能保护膝盖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死盯死思」——双脚站定、对方说什么也不让步，就是立场；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stare（站立）→ 拉丁语 constantia（坚定站立，词根 stant-）→ 古法语 estance（站立、停留）→ 中古英语 estance → 现代英语 stance（先指站姿，后指立场）。

sensesIntro.en: Stance starts from the body standing still, spreads to the viewpoint a person refuses to move from, then to sport postures, hard opposition, and an old sense of a place to stay.
sensesIntro.cn: stance 从身体站定出发，发展为不愿挪动半步的观点立场，再分出运动架势、强硬对立姿态，以及「歇脚之处」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet planted wide, the whole body standing its ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚分开踩稳，整个人在原处站定不让。

branches.en: The physical way of standing is the base sense.
branches.cn: 身体的站姿是最基础的义项。

branches.en: Where one stands becomes what one stands for.
branches.cn: 站在哪里，逐渐变成主张什么。

branches.en: Sports use the word for ready positions.
branches.cn: 体育领域用它指预备姿势。

branches.en: A stance on an issue sharpens into hard opposition.
branches.cn: 对某事的立场一旦摆开，就会变成强硬的对立姿态。

branches.en: The old sense of a standing place survives only in history.
branches.cn: 「站立之处」的旧义如今只留在历史文本中。

intro.en: Stance has no English prefix of its own, but it is built on the Latin standing root stant- and shares its family with constant, substance, and circumstance.
intro.cn: stance 本身不带英语前缀，但建立在拉丁语「站立」词根 stant- 之上，与 constant、substance、circumstance 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare means to stand, and its participle stans supplies stant- to a long line of English words from constant to substance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，其分词 stans 提供 stant- 这一成分，养活了从 constant 到 substance 的一大批英语词。

items.example: Stare is the source of the whole standing family.
items.exampleCN: stare 是整个「站立」词族的源头。

items.example: The root stant appears in constant and in stance.
items.exampleCN: 词根 stant 出现在 constant 与 stance 中。

items.example: Constantia gives English constancy.
items.exampleCN: constantia 演变为英语 constancy。

items.meaning: way of standing; position on an issue
items.example: Stance keeps standing and opinion together.
items.exampleCN: stance 把「站」和「主张」合在一处。

items.example: The prefix con- carries the sense of standing together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 带来「一起站住」的意思。

items.example: Constant is stance with a fixed purpose.
items.exampleCN: constant 是「站定不变」的形容词。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the root underneath.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把词根放到下面。

items.meaningCN: 站于其下的东西，即物质、实质
items.example: Substance joins sub- to the standing root.
items.exampleCN: substance 把 sub- 与站立词根接在一起。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ance names a state or quality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 表示某种状态或性质。

items.example: The prefix circum- gives circumstance.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 circum- 构成 circumstance。

definition_zh: 订书机；订书钉；主要产品（或大宗商品）；把书页装订起来的人
definition_en: a small device that drives a thin metal wire through paper to hold the sheets together, or a heavy wire fastening itself
core_image: 桌上一个手掌大小的金属小机器，啪的一声把一枚细铁丝钉穿进纸里
scene: 复印室的桌角，一叠刚打印好的讲义还散在风里，纸张随时要被吹走。She pressed the stapler down hard and the corner of every sheet clicked shut.
sceneCN: 这里 stapler 是「订书机」（第 2 个义项：压手柄把金属丝扎进纸里的办公工具）；句意为她用力压下令订书机，每一张纸的边角都咔哒一声合上。画面里能辨认的东西：金属机身、一叠讲义、纸角上露出的铁丝钉。

pos.zh: 名词：订书机、订书钉、装订工、主要商品
形容词性的定语：用在名词前，如订书机业务、主要商品这类说法

collocations.zh: 长臂订书机（可订册子中缝）

derivatives.zh: 由本词减去 -er 得到的基词：名词义为「订书钉、主要产品、主食」，动词义为「用订书钉钉住」
由基词动词 staple 加 -ing 构成，义为「装订、钉住」；与本词共用同一基词
形近但词源不同：来自 stake「木桩」，义为「用桩固定的」；只是拼写相近

senses.title: A thin wire fastening
senses.definition: a short piece of wire bent like a U, pressed through paper or cloth and folded over at the back
senses.definitionCN: 弯成 U 形的短金属丝，穿过纸张或布料后在背面折倒固定
senses.example: He fixed the two pages with a single staple and then filed the sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一枚订书钉把两页纸固定好，然后把纸归档。
senses.why: In Middle English a staple was a wire loop driven into a post into which a bolt was dropped; the short bent wire is this loop reduced to paper size.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语的 staple 原指敲进木柱里、用来插门闩的铁环；订书钉就是这种铁环缩小到纸张尺度后的样子。

senses.title: Press tool that drives the wire
senses.definition: a spring-loaded office tool that pushes a staple through sheets of paper and folds its legs flat
senses.definitionCN: 靠弹簧动作把订书钉压穿纸页、并把钉脚压平的办公工具
senses.example: The folder came apart because the stapler was empty.
senses.exampleCN: 文件夹散开了，因为订书机里没有钉了。
senses.why: The noun of a repeated action often takes -er, and here the action is joining sheets with staples, so the device that does it is the stapler.
senses.whyCN: 表示重复动作的名词常加 -er 表示工具或人；这里动作是用订书钉把纸连起来，做这件事的器械就是 stapler。

senses.title: A main product or commodity
senses.definition: an item traded or produced in large and steady amounts, such as a basic good or a leading product
senses.definitionCN: 大量而稳定生产或交易的商品，如基本货物或主营产品
senses.example: Wheat has long been a staple of the region and of its export trade.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦长期以来既是该地区的主要农产品，也是它的出口大宗货品。
senses.why: The word first named a fixed market or a place where goods were always sold; that fixedness went from the place to the goods always kept there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指固定的交易市场以及人们总是在那里出售的货物；这种「固定」从地点转移到了常备的货品上。

senses.title: A basic food eaten regularly
senses.definition: a basic food, such as rice, bread, or potatoes, that is eaten regularly and makes up much of the diet
senses.definitionCN: 常吃的主粮，如米、面包或土豆，构成日常饮食的大部分
senses.example: For millions of families, rice is the daily staple.
senses.exampleCN: 对数百万家庭来说，大米是每日主食。
senses.why: This is the commodity sense narrowed to the kitchen table: the food that is always kept in store and always eaten.
senses.whyCN: 这是「大宗商品」义缩小到餐桌上：总是常备、总是被吃的食物。

senses.title: The main or typical element
senses.definition: the main or most usual part of something, such as the subject of conversation, writing, or performance
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中最主要或最常见的部分，如谈论、写作或演出的题材
senses.example: Flooding is a staple of local weather reports in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春季洪水是当地天气报道的常客。
senses.why: What is always present in a warehouse is also what is always present in talk or in art; the fixedness carries over into ideas.
senses.whyCN: 仓库里总有的东西，也是话题和作品里总会出现的东西；这种「固定常在」延伸到了观念上。

senses.title: A town where wool was traded
senses.definition: a town appointed as the official market for wool and other goods, used especially in medieval England
senses.definitionCN: 经指定作为羊毛等货物官方交易地的市镇，尤见于中世纪的英格兰
senses.example: Wool was sold only in a staple, so the legal market and the word agree.
senses.exampleCN: 羊毛只能在指定的羊毛市场出售，所以合法的市场与这个词的含义是一致的。
senses.why: The oldest recorded meaning is a market place with a fixed site and fixed goods; this is where the whole family begins.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早涵义是地点固定、货物固定的市场；整个词族的起点就在这里。

senses.title: To fasten with a staple
senses.definition: to fasten papers or materials together with one or more staples
senses.definitionCN: 用一个或多个订书钉把纸张或材料固定在一起
senses.example: Please staple the receipt to the form before you file it.
senses.exampleCN: 归档前请把收据钉在表格上。
senses.why: The verb turns the metal wire into an action: the little loop is the tool, and driving it through is the motion.
senses.whyCN: 动词把金属丝变成动作：小铁环是工具，把它压穿过去就是动作本身。

senses.title: Inside a staple gun
senses.titleCN: 钉枪里的 U 形钉
senses.definition: the heavy U-shaped wire that a staple gun drives into wood, cloth, or packaging
senses.definitionCN: 钉枪射入木材、布料或包装的粗大 U 形金属钉
senses.example: Each staple in the box is thick enough to hold the boards together.
senses.exampleCN: 盒里每一枚大号钉都够粗，能把木板固定住。
senses.why: The industrial staple is the same bent wire scaled up: the post-and-bolt loop of the old word reappears in carpentry.
senses.whyCN: 工业用的订钉就是同一种弯铁丝放大后的版本：古义里「柱与闩」的铁环在木工里重新出现。

intro.en: Stapler meaning the paper tool is a modern agent noun built on staple; the whole family starts with staple as a post, a bolt loop and a fixed wool market.
intro.cn: 表示订书机的 stapler 是近代由 staple 加 -er 构成的名词；整个词族始于 staple 的「柱子」「门闩铁环」和「官定羊毛市场」三个古义。

items.en: The word is generally connected with Old English stapol, a post or pillar, and with Old French estaple, a market. Whether English borrowed the market word from Low Dutch or the other way round is disputed, so the exact route is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词与古英语 stapol「柱子」以及古法语 estaple「市场」相关；市场义究竟是英语借自低地荷兰语，还是荷兰语借自英语，学界有争议，确切路径来源不确定。

items.en: Staple first names a post; then the wire loop driven into a post, into which a door bolt drops; and also a fixed trading town.
items.cn: 中古英语的 staple 先指柱子，再指钉进柱子、供门闩落入的铁环，同时也指固定的贸易市镇。

items.en: Statutes appointed certain towns as staples where wool and other goods could be sold; the fixed place gave the word its lasting image of something always in store. First dates for each sense are uncertain.
items.cn: 法令指定若干市镇为 wool staple，羊毛等货物只能在那些地方出售；固定的地点给这个词留下了「常备仓库」的持久意象。各义项的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word moves from the market to its contents: a staple becomes a main commodity, then a main food such as bread, and later the usual subject of a talk or a show.
items.cn: 词义从「市场」转向「货物」：staple 先指主要商品，再指面包一类主粮，后来又指谈话或节目惯用的题材。

items.en: The short bent wire for fastening paper revives the old loop sense; the tool is staple plus -er, and paper, reports and booklets follow.
items.cn: 装订纸张的弯短铁丝复活了古老的「铁环」义；工具就是 staple 加 -er，随后纸张、报告与小册子都离不开它。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base word, the sound-alike verbs and the two tools that push metal; the near-meaning group gathers paper fasteners and ordinary food staples.
note.cn: 形近组收基词、读音相近的动词以及两种打钉工具；近义组收各类纸张固定工具与日常主食。

entries.definition: The wire, the main product, or the basic food; also the verb meaning to fasten with wire.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「订书钉、主要产品、主食」，兼作动词「用钉钉住」；是 stapler 的基词。

entries.definition: A hand-held tool that fires heavy staples into wood or fabric; a stapler in name but not on a desk.
entries.definitionCN: 手持工具，会把粗大的 U 形钉射入木材或织物；虽与 stapler 同源，却不是办公桌上那种订书机。

entries.definition: A misspelling of staple with a doubled p; not a real English word.
entries.definitionCN: 把 staple 多写一个 p 的错误拼法，并非真实的英语单词，只用来提醒注意拼写。

entries.definition: A bent wire clip that holds sheets without piercing them, so the pages can be taken apart again.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「回形针」，靠夹住而不穿透纸张来固定，可以随时拆开。

entries.definition: A tool that makes holes in paper so the sheets can be held in a ring binder.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「打孔机」，在纸上打孔，以便把纸装进环形夹里。

entries.definition: A basic food made from flour and baked; a classic staple of the table in many places.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「面包」，由面粉烘焙而成，是许多地方餐桌上的经典主食。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below use the real history of staple and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 staple 的真实词史，以及这个词实际出现的日常搭配。

normal.en: The -er is the tool suffix: staple the wire plus -er gives the stapler that drives the wire.
normal.cn: -er 是表工具的构词后缀：staple（订书钉）加 -er 就成了压钉的 stapler。

normal.en: A staple was once a loop in a post for a door bolt; a paper staple is the same loop made small.
normal.cn: staple 原指木柱上给门闩用的铁环；纸上的订书钉就是同一个铁环做小了。

normal.en: A staple food is the food always kept in store, like rice or bread.
normal.cn: staple food 就是家里常备的主食，比如米或面包。

normal.en: A staple gun uses the same name as the stapler but fires much heavier wire into wood.
normal.cn: staple gun 与 stapler 同名，但它射出的是粗得多的钉，扎进木头。

normal.en: Compare paper clip: a clip holds sheets without piercing them, a staple goes right through.
normal.cn: 对比 paper clip：回形针夹住纸张、不穿透，订书钉则直接穿透。

abstract.en: Picture a palm of your hand pressing down on a small metal shell while the corners meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌按下小小的金属外壳，两张纸的边角就此对齐。

abstract.en: Think of a wire bent into a U, like a tiny bridge of feet two steps through paper and stops.
abstract.cn: 想一根弯成 U 形的铁丝，像两只小脚跨过纸张，落地便停住。

abstract.en: See a warehouse that always keeps the same goods at the front door; those goods are the staple.
abstract.cn: 想象一间仓库总把同样的货品堆在门口；这些货就是 staple。

examples.en: The stapler on my desk has run out of staples again.
examples.cn: 我桌上的订书机又没钉了。

examples.en: He asked for a stapler to bind the twenty-page report.
examples.cn: 他要来一台订书机，好把二十页的报告订好。

examples.en: Millet is a staple in many dry regions of northern China.
examples.cn: 小米是中国北方许多干旱地区的主食。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四袋碰」——四袋纸使劲往一起碰，再按下手柄，纸角就订住了；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为与古英语 stapol「柱子、台阶」同源，也可能经低地荷兰语传入；由「柱子上的门闩铁环」到「固定的贸易市场」，再到「常备货品与主食」，最后到「订书钉与订书机」。词根路径的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The family runs from the fixed place to the fixed goods and finally to the small wire: a wire fastening, the press tool that drives it, a main commodity, a basic food, the usual element of anything, the official wool market, the act of fastening, and the heavy industrial staple.
sensesIntro.cn: 这一族从「固定的地点」走到「常备的货物」，最后落到「小小的铁丝」：铁丝钉、压钉工具、大宗商品、主粮、任何事物的惯用内容、官定羊毛市场、钉住的动作，以及工业用的大号钉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small metal press slams a U-shaped wire through a stack of paper and folds it flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台小小的金属压机把 U 形铁丝压穿一叠纸，再把两端压平。

branches.en: THE WIRE: the short bent staple is the oldest loop reduced to paper size.
branches.cn: 铁丝线：弯短的订书钉是古老铁环缩小到纸张尺度后的样子。

branches.en: THE TOOL AND THE ACT: the -er noun names the device, the verb names driving the wire.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：-er 名词指器械，动词则指把铁丝压进去。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a fixed trading town becomes the goods always traded there, then the food always eaten there.
branches.cn: 市场线：固定的贸易市镇变成总在那里交易的货品，再变成总在那里吃的主食。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: what is always present in goods becomes what is always present in talk or art.
branches.cn: 惯例线：货品里总有的东西，也成了话题或作品里总会出现的东西。

branches.en: BOTH ENDS: the oldest sense is the fixed wool market, the newest machine sense lives in a staple gun.
branches.cn: 两端线：最早之义是固定的羊毛市场，最新的机器义则活在钉枪里。

intro.en: Stapler is staple plus the agent suffix -er; the family reaches back through Old English stapol and Old French estaple, and English then builds compounds such as staple food and staple gun.
intro.cn: stapler 由 staple 加表人或工具的后缀 -er 构成；这一族可上溯到古英语 stapol 与古法语 estaple，英语再用 staple food、staple gun 等复合词扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin stapula and Old French estaple are recorded in the market sense; their deeper link with Old English stapol is generally assumed but not proven.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 stapula 与古法语 estaple 都有「市场」一义；它们与古英语 stapol 的更深联系只是普遍假设，尚未被确证。

items.meaning: a wire fastener, a main product, a basic food
items.example: Staple is the base on which every other form is built.
items.exampleCN: staple 是其余一切形式所依托的基词。

items.meaning: a person or instrument that does something
items.example: The suffix -er turns staple into a tool name.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 staple 变成工具的名称。

items.example: Staplers in the library are shared by every class.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆的订书机由各班共用。

items.example: To staple a report is to finish binding it.
items.exampleCN: 把报告钉好，装订就算完成。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing
items.example: Stapling pages takes only a second.
items.exampleCN: 钉住书页只需一秒钟。

items.example: The compound keeps the main-goods sense at the table.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「主要货品」义带到了餐桌上。

items.meaning: a tool that fires heavy staples
items.example: The compound shows the tool sense scaled up.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词显示工具义被放大了。

items.meaning: goods traded in large and steady amounts
items.example: The compound returns the main-goods sense to trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「主要货品」义又带回贸易。

items.example: The compound names the industrial version of the tool.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指这一工具的工业版。

definition_zh: 淀粉；含淀粉的食物；浆洗（衣物使硬挺）；拘谨、古板
definition_en: a white carbohydrate stored in plants such as potatoes, rice and wheat, or a stiffening agent made from it and used on cloth
core_image: 一块切开的土豆断面上白白的浆粉，摸上去有细微的颗粒感
scene: 厨房的案板上，刚切开的土豆还挂着乳白色的汁液，手指一抹，就留下薄薄一层白色的粉。A thin layer of starch dried on the knife blade after the potatoes were sliced.
sceneCN: 这里 starch 是「淀粉」（第 1 个义项：植物储藏的白色碳水化合物）；句意为土豆切片之后，刀刃上留下一层干了淀粉。画面上可辨认的东西：案板、切开的土豆、刀口上的白粉。

pos.zh: 名词：淀粉；含淀粉的食物；浆衣用的浆糊
及物动词：给衣物上浆，使其硬挺

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「含淀粉的；拘谨古板的」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「不含淀粉的」，属不常用的组合
由 starchy 加名词后缀构成，义为「含淀粉的性质；僵硬、古板」
由本词加动词词尾构成，作形容词义为「上过浆的、硬挺的」

senses.title: The white carbohydrate in plants
senses.titleCN: 淀粉（植物储藏的碳水化合物）
senses.definition: a white, tasteless carbohydrate made by green plants and stored in seeds, roots and tubers such as wheat, rice and potatoes
senses.definitionCN: 绿色植物制造的白色无味碳水化合物，储存在小麦、稻米、土豆等种子与块茎中
senses.example: Potatoes contain a lot of starch, which is released when they are boiled.
senses.exampleCN: 土豆含有大量淀粉，煮熟时这些淀粉会释放出来。
senses.why: The word comes from a Germanic root meaning strong, and the earliest use was the stiffening substance pressed from grain and potatoes, so the plant store and the paste carry one name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「强壮、坚固」的日耳曼语词根，最早的用法指从谷物与土豆中压出的硬挺物质，所以植物中的储藏物和浆糊共用一个名字。

senses.title: A pulp for stiffening cloth
senses.definition: a pasty preparation of starch and water used to make fabric, especially collars and cuffs, smooth and stiff
senses.definitionCN: 淀粉与水调成的浆糊，用于让布料光滑硬挺，尤其是衣领和袖口
senses.example: The nurse mixed starch with cold water before ironing the caps.
senses.exampleCN: 护士先把淀粉调进冷水，再熨烫那些帽子。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded use: boiled starch turns liquid when wet and dries hard, and the strength of the paste gave the word its name.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早有记录的用义：煮过的淀粉湿时流动、干后变硬，浆糊的「强固」正是这个词得名的原因。

senses.title: Food made with starch
senses.definition: foods rich in starch, such as bread, potatoes, rice, and pasta, often counted as carbohydrates in a diet
senses.definitionCN: 富含淀粉的食物，如面包、土豆、米饭、面食，在饮食中常归为碳水化合物
senses.example: You can eat starch in the evening without gaining weight if the portion is small.
senses.exampleCN: 如果分量不大，晚上吃淀粉类食物也不会发胖。
senses.why: In nutrition the substance stands for the foods that carry it: to eat starch is to eat the plant store itself.
senses.whyCN: 在营养学里，物质代替了含有它的食物：eat starch 就是吃下植物储存的那份能量。

senses.title: To treat cloth with starch
senses.definition: to put starch on fabric, especially clothes, so that it becomes stiff and holds its shape
senses.definitionCN: 把淀粉涂在布料上，尤其衣物，使其硬挺并保持形状
senses.example: She starched his shirt every Sunday for the weekly meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 每个星期天为周会，她都把他衬衫上浆熨挺。
senses.why: The noun turns into the action of putting the stiffening paste where it is needed.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动作，指把硬挺的浆糊加到需要的地方。

senses.title: Stiff and formal behaviour
senses.definition: a stiff, formal, or old-fashioned way of speaking or behaving, often in the phrase stiff with starch
senses.definitionCN: 说话或举止僵硬、拘谨、过时的样子，常用于 stiff with starch 这类说法
senses.example: His letters were stiff with starch and full of long, cold sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 他的信写得拘谨古板，满篇都是又长又冷的句子。
senses.why: Starched cloth holds a shape and does not bend, and this image is used for people whose manner will not bend either.
senses.whyCN: 上过浆的布料固定形状、不会弯折；这一意象也被用到举止不肯变通的人身上。

intro.en: Starch has the same Germanic origin as stark and stiff, and the earliest sense was the paste that made linen stand up.
intro.cn: starch 与 stark、stiff 同出日耳曼语源，最早的义项就是让亚麻布硬挺起来的浆糊。

items.en: The preferred view links starch to the root reconstructed as *starkaz, strong or stiff, the same family as stark. The root shape is a reconstruction and the details are source uncertain.
items.cn: 较为通行的观点把 starch 追溯到重构形式 *starkaz「强壮、僵硬」，与 stark 同族；词根形态属于重构，更深一层的最早形态来源不确定。

items.en: A form close to stercan or styrcan is generally assumed to lie behind the word, but the exact Old English shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为该词背后有近似 stercan 或 styrcan 的古英语形式，但确切的古英语形态不确定。

items.en: The word first names the paste used in stiffening linen; the plant product behind the paste is the same thing and gets the same name.
items.cn: 这个词最初指浆洗亚麻布用的浆糊；浆糊背后那种植物产物是同一件东西，于是得到同一个名字。

items.en: Chemistry takes the word over for the carbohydrate revealed by the iodine test, and the food sense follows in the kitchen.
items.cn: 化学把这个词接过去指碘测试显露的碳水化合物，食物义随后也在厨房里成长起来。

items.en: The image of stiff cloth becomes a figure for stiff manners, and the word then settles into nutrition, textiles, food science and daily speech.
items.cn: 「僵硬布料」的意象转喻为僵硬举止，此后这个词定居在营养学、纺织、食品科学与日常口语中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and verbs built on the same root of stiffness; the near-meaning group separates the main plant store from sugars, fibre and protein.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「硬挺」词根构成的形容词与动词；近义组把主要植物储藏物同糖、纤维与蛋白质区分开。

entries.definition: Containing starch, or stiff and formal in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含淀粉的」，引申为「拘谨、古板的」；由本词加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Treated with starch so that it is stiff, said of cloth or of a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上过浆的、硬挺的」，可指布料，也可形容举止。

entries.definition: Stiff, rigid, or bare and harsh; a cousin from the same Germanic root of stiffness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「僵硬的、赤裸而严酷的」；与 starch 同出表示「硬挺」的日耳曼语词根。

entries.definition: A sweet soluble carbohydrate; smaller and sweeter than starch and quick to dissolve.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「糖」，可溶且带甜味的碳水化合物，比淀粉分子小、溶解快。

entries.definition: Plant material that the body cannot digest; starch is digested but fibre is not.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「膳食纤维」，人体无法消化的植物成分；淀粉能被消化，纤维则不能。

entries.definition: A nutrient built from long chains of amino acids; paired with starch as the two main building blocks of food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛋白质」，由氨基酸长链构成，与淀粉并列为食物的两大主要成分。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below use the real root of stiffness and the phrases in which the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「硬挺」词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Starch, stark and stiff share the sense of standing rigid, so starch is the substance that makes cloth stand up.
normal.cn: starch、stark 与 stiff 都带「僵直不动」的意思，所以 starch 就是让布料立起来的物质。

normal.en: A starched collar holds its shape all day, exactly as starch holds the shape of a shirt.
normal.cn: 上过浆的衣领整天保持形状，正如 starch 固定住衬衫的轮廓。

normal.en: Iodine turns starch blue, a classic test in the school laboratory.
normal.cn: 碘遇淀粉变蓝，这是学校实验室里的经典测试。

normal.en: Starchy foods such as bread and rice give energy slowly because they break down step by step.
normal.cn: 面包、米饭这类 starchy foods 会逐步分解，因此缓慢供能。

normal.en: Compare sugar: sugar is short and sweet, starch is long and slow.
normal.cn: 对比 sugar：糖短而甜，淀粉长而慢。

abstract.en: See a boiled potato cooling on a plate, its cut face turning glassy and hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一只煮熟的土豆在盘子里放凉，切面变得光亮而坚硬。

abstract.en: Think of a laundered collar standing upright like a small white wall around the neck.
abstract.cn: 想一条洗过上浆的衣领，像一堵小小的白墙，围着脖子立着。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon dipped into white powder that squeaks slightly under the thumb.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子伸进白色粉末里，粉末在手指下发出轻微的吱吱声。

examples.en: Corn starch thickens the soup much faster than flour does.
examples.cn: 玉米淀粉比面粉更快让汤变得浓稠。

examples.en: The hotel starched its pillowcases so that they cracked when folded.
examples.cn: 酒店把枕套上浆，折起来时会发出脆响。

examples.en: Scientists tested the starch content of ten different types of rice.
examples.cn: 科学家测定了十种不同稻米的淀粉含量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯打赤」——把衬衫袖口使劲一打，浆得硬挺发赤；这是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自日耳曼语重构形式 *starkaz「强、硬」，与 stark、stiff 同族；古英语中近似 stercan 的形式不确定；由「使人硬挺的浆糊」到「植物中的淀粉」，再到「淀粉类食物」与引申的「拘谨古板」。

sensesIntro.en: Starch begins as a stiffening paste and widens into the plant carbohydrate, the foods that carry it, the act of stiffening cloth, and finally a stiff manner.
sensesIntro.cn: starch 从使衣物硬挺的浆糊起家，扩展到植物中的碳水化合物、承载它的食物、给布料上浆的动作，最后引申为僵硬的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut potato shows a white, slightly gritty paste inside, and that paste dries hard.
core.cn: 核心意象：切开的土豆里露出白色、略带颗粒的浆糊状物质，这层浆糊干后变硬。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the white store in roots and seeds carries the name of the paste.
branches.cn: 植物线：根和种子里的白色储藏物沿用了浆糊的名字。

branches.en: THE CLOTH: the paste and the act of applying it keep the oldest sense, stiffness.
branches.cn: 布料线：浆糊本身与上浆的动作保留了最古老的「硬挺」义。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: the substance stands for the foods made of it, such as bread and rice.
branches.cn: 厨房线：物质代替了由它做成的食物，如面包和米饭。

branches.en: THE MANNER: cloth that will not bend becomes a person whose manner will not bend.
branches.cn: 举止线：不肯弯折的布料，变成了不肯弯折的举止。

branches.en: Laboratory and table meet: the plant store measured in a tube is the same store eaten on a plate.
branches.cn: 实验室与餐桌在此相接：试管里测的植物储藏物，就是盘子里吃下的那部分。

intro.en: Starch is a short Germanic word; English adds -y, -ed and -less, and compounds such as corn starch extend the family.
intro.cn: starch 是一个简短的日耳曼词；英语加 -y、-ed、-less 扩展它，corn starch 这类复合词也在扩展这一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin had amylum for starch, and the scientific name of starch amylum descends from it, although starch itself is not a Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 amylum 表示淀粉，淀粉的科学名 amylum 即由此而来；但 starch 本身并非拉丁词。

items.example: The noun keeps both the kitchen and the laundry senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留厨房与洗衣房两种含义。

items.meaning: full of, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -y forms starchy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 starchy。

items.meaning: past, or having the state of
items.example: The suffix -ed forms starched, which describes cloth after treatment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 starched，用来描述处理过的布料。

items.example: Starching shirts was once a weekly chore.
items.exampleCN: 给衬衫上浆曾是每周的家务。

items.example: The suffix -less forms starchless, which is a rare word.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 starchless，但这个词少见。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms starchiness from starchy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 由 starchy 构成 starchiness。

items.meaning: starch from maize, used in cooking
items.example: The compound names the most common cooking form.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指最常用的烹饪用淀粉。

items.example: The compound carries the food sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词承载食物义。

items.example: The Latin noun gave science the name amylum.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词给了科学术语 amylum。

definition_zh: 含淀粉的；淀粉质的；（举止、言谈）拘谨的、古板的
definition_en: containing a lot of starch, or stiff and formal in manner
core_image: 一盘切好的土豆和米饭，颜色发白，看上去干干的、带粉末感
scene: 学校食堂的餐盘里，土豆、米饭和面包堆成一座白色的小山，旁边只有几片青菜。The lunch was so starchy that the students asked for more vegetables the next day.
sceneCN: 这里 starchy 是「含淀粉的」（第 1 个义项：含大量淀粉的食物）；句意为午餐淀粉太多，学生们第二天要求多给些蔬菜。画面上可辨认的东西：餐盘、土豆块、米饭、面包、青菜。

pos.zh: 形容词：含淀粉的；淀粉质的；拘谨古板的

derivatives.zh: 由本词减去形容词后缀 -y 得到的基词：名词义为「淀粉、浆糊」，动词义为「上浆」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「含淀粉的性质；僵硬、古板」
与基词动词形式相关的形容词，义为「上过浆的、硬挺的」

senses.title: Full of starch as food
senses.definition: containing a lot of starch, said of foods such as potatoes, rice, bread and pasta
senses.definitionCN: 含有大量淀粉的，用于形容土豆、米饭、面包、面食这类食物
senses.example: Doctors suggest eating less starchy food and more green vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议少吃含淀粉的食物，多吃绿叶蔬菜。
senses.why: The suffix -y means full of, so potato or maize that is full of starch is simply starchy; the adjective is the noun plus one letter.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 表示「充满」，所以充满淀粉的土豆、玉米就是 starchy；这个形容词只是名词多了一点。

senses.title: Of or resembling starch
senses.definition: made of starch or tasting and feeling like starch, such as a paste, a powder or a sauce
senses.definitionCN: 由淀粉制成的，或在口味和质感上像淀粉的，如浆糊、粉末或酱汁
senses.example: The sauce went starchy and dull after it stood too long on the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁在炉子上放久了，变得发粉发木。
senses.why: Once -y attaches to a substance name, the adjective can describe anything that has the quality of that substance rather than the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 -y 附着在物质名词上，形容词就可以描述具有那种性质的东西，而不必是那种物质本身。

senses.title: Stiff and old-fashioned in manner
senses.definition: formal, stiff, and rather old-fashioned in behaviour, speech, or style, without warmth or ease
senses.definitionCN: 行为、言语或风格正式僵硬、有些过时，缺少亲切与自然
senses.example: The tailor was starchy but fair, and everyone respected him.
senses.exampleCN: 那位裁缝很古板，但为人公道，大家都敬重他。
senses.why: Starched cloth is stiff and unbending, and the same picture is used for a person who will not unbend in company.
senses.whyCN: 上过浆的布料僵硬、不肯弯折，同样的画面被用在不肯在人群前放松下来的人身上。

intro.en: Starchy is simply the noun starch with the English suffix -y; the stiff manner comes from the older picture of starched linen, not from the plant itself.
intro.cn: starchy 只是名词 starch 加英语后缀 -y；表示「拘谨」的义项来自上浆亚麻布的画面，而不是来自植物本身。

items.en: The base starch is generally traced to the root reconstructed as *starkaz, strong or stiff, and is usually connected with stark. The root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 基词 starch 一般认为可追溯到重构形式 *starkaz「强壮、僵硬」，并常与 stark 联系起来；词根形态属于重构。

items.en: Starch, the stiffening paste for linen, is first recorded in the fifteenth century; its exact Old English ancestor is uncertain.
items.cn: 表示浆洗亚麻布用浆糊的 starch 在十五世纪首次有记录；其确切的古英语前身不确定。

items.en: The suffix -y, meaning full of, is added to the noun; starchy first describes cloth and household preparations full of starch.
items.cn: 表「充满」的后缀 -y 加在名词之上；starchy 最早形容充满淀粉的布料与家用制剂。

items.en: With the rise of chemistry and nutrition the adjective settles into food writing: starchy foods, starchy roots, starchy diet. First dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 随着化学与营养学的兴起，这个形容词定居在食品写作中：starchy foods、starchy roots、starchy diet。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The picture of stiff starched cloth is extended to people, and starchy comes to mean formal and unbending in manner.
items.cn: 硬挺上浆布料的画面被延伸到人身上，starchy 于是表示举止正式、不肯变通。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base noun, its verb forms and the related adjective; the near-meaning group separates sweet sugars, soft textures and informal manners from the starchy picture.
note.cn: 形近组收基词、它的动词形式与相关形容词；近义组把甜味糖、软糯口感与随和举止同「淀粉感」区分开。

entries.definition: The carbohydrate itself, or the paste used to stiffen cloth; also the verb to treat cloth with it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「淀粉、浆糊」，兼作动词「上浆」；是本词的基词。

entries.definition: Stiffened with starch, especially of shirts, collars and cuffs.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上过浆的、硬挺的」，尤指衬衫、衣领与袖口。

entries.definition: The quality of being starchy, either in food or in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「淀粉感」，也可指拘谨古板的气质。

entries.definition: Full of sugar and tasting sweet; the sugary sweet pair is the opposite of the starchy food pair.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含糖的、甜的」，与 starchy 同属食物口感形容，但方向相反。

entries.definition: Soft, dry and powder-covered like flour, said of potatoes or textures.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粉质的、面粉般的」，用来形容土豆的口感或质地的干爽。

entries.definition: Extremely neat and formal in dress and behaviour, too correct to be relaxed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一本正经的、拘谨的」，衣着举止过于规整，难以放松。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below work from the suffix -y, the base word starch and the picture of starched cloth.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子围绕后缀 -y、基词 starch 以及上浆布料的画面展开。

normal.en: Starch plus y is starchy, just as salt plus y is salty and starch plus y means full of starch.
normal.cn: starch 加 y 就成了 starchy，就像 salt 加 y 是 salty 一样，意思是「充满淀粉的」。

normal.en: Starchy foods are the ones that give slow energy: bread, rice, potatoes, noodles.
normal.cn: starchy foods 是缓慢供能的那类食物：面包、米饭、土豆、面条。

normal.en: Compare salty, sugary, spicy: starchy belongs to the same family of taste and texture adjectives.
normal.cn: 对比 salty、sugary、spicy：starchy 属于同一类味道与质地的形容词。

normal.en: A starchy manner is a starched manner: correct, upright and unable to unbend.
normal.cn: starchy manner 就是 starched manner：端正、笔直、弯不下来。

normal.en: Compare salty and sugary: the -y suffix always means full of, so starchy means full of starch.
normal.cn: 对比 salty 和 sugary：-y 后缀总是表示「充满」，所以 starchy 就是充满淀粉的。

abstract.en: See a plate piled high with white rice and potatoes, shining and slightly sticky.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘堆得很高的白米饭和土豆，泛着光、微微发黏。

abstract.en: Think of a spoon lifted out of thick sauce, making a soft, doughy sound.
abstract.cn: 想一把勺子从浓稠的酱汁里提起来，发出软糯的声音。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a white starched collar who bows too correctly to everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一位戴着白色上浆硬领的先生，对每个人都过分端正地鞠躬。

examples.en: The children ate too much starchy food and wanted a nap.
examples.cn: 孩子们吃了太多含淀粉的食物，想睡午觉。

examples.en: This soup is starchy and thick, almost like porridge.
examples.cn: 这汤淀粉很重、很稠，几乎像粥。

examples.en: Behind the polished counter stood a starchy man in a dark suit.
examples.cn: 光亮的柜台后站着一位穿深色西装、举止拘谨的男人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯打气」——把土豆打成气鼓鼓的粉团，满是淀粉；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由日耳曼语源的 starch（一般认为追溯至重构形式 *starkaz「强、硬」，与 stark 同族）加英语形容词后缀 -y 构成，本义「充满淀粉的」；再由上浆硬挺布料的意象引申出「拘谨古板的」。

sensesIntro.en: Starchy has three faces: food full of starch, a texture or taste that recalls starch, and a manner as stiff and unbending as starched cloth.
sensesIntro.cn: starchy 有三副面孔：充满淀粉的食物、让人想到淀粉的质地与口感，以及像上浆布料那样僵硬不肯变通的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate of sliced potatoes and rice, pale and powdery, filling the plate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘切开的土豆和米饭，颜色发白、带粉感，堆满整个盘子。

branches.en: THE PLATE: food full of starch is the everyday and most common sense.
branches.cn: 餐盘线：充满淀粉的食物是最日常、最常见的义项。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a paste or powder that feels like starch shows the same quality outside food.
branches.cn: 表面线：摸起来像淀粉的浆糊或粉末，在食物之外显现同样的质感。

branches.en: THE PERSON: starched cloth becomes a description of a person who cannot unbend.
branches.cn: 人物线：上过浆的布料变成了对不肯放松之人的描写。

branches.en: Coverage and texture: the sense is either containing starch or having starch qualities.
branches.cn: 含量与似然：一义是含有淀粉，一义是具有像淀粉的性质。

branches.en: One suffix makes both a kitchen word and a character word out of a single noun.
branches.cn: 同一个后缀从同一个名词里造出了厨房词和性格词。

intro.en: Starchy is a short derivative: the base noun starch, the adjective suffix -y, and the further nouns and adjectives that grow from it.
intro.cn: starchy 是一个简短的派生词：基词名词 starch 加形容词后缀 -y，再从这里长出别的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Starch is not a Latin word, but Latin amylum names the same substance and supplies the scientific vocabulary of amyl in chemistry and food science.
latinIntro.cn: starch 并非拉丁语单词，但拉丁语 amylum 指同一物质，并为化学与食品科学提供了 amyl 这一学术词根。

items.meaning: the plant carbohydrate, the stiffening paste
items.example: Starch is the base that the adjective builds on.
items.exampleCN: starch 是这个形容词所依托的基词。

items.example: The suffix -y turns salt into salty and starch into starchy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 salt 变成 salty，把 starch 变成 starchy。

items.example: The suffix -ier forms starchier.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ier 构成 starchier。

items.example: The suffix -iest forms starchiest.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -iest 构成 starchiest。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms starchiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 starchiness。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms starched, as in a starched collar.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 starched，如 a starched collar。

items.example: The compound fixes the everyday food sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词组固定了日常的食物义。

items.example: The element amyl- appears in scientific terms for starch.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 amyl- 出现在表示淀粉的科学术语里。

definition_zh: 海星；星鱼
definition_en: a flat sea animal shaped like a star, with five or more arms that can slowly pull it along the seabed
core_image: 浅海礁石上摊开的一枚五角星，腕尖贴着沙面慢慢挪动
scene: 退潮后的礁石池里，一枚海星紧贴着湿滑的石面一动不动。On the wet rocks of a tidal pool, a starfish clings to the stone without moving.
sceneCN: 这里 starfish 是「海星」（第 1 个义项：身体呈星形的海洋动物）；句意：退潮后的礁石池里，一枚海星紧贴着湿滑的石面一动不动。

derivatives.zh: 由名词 starfish 与分词 shaped 复合而成，义为「星形的」
由名词 starfish 加动名词后缀 -ing 构成的少见用法，指在潮间采集海星的活动
由名词 starfish 加形容词后缀 -y 构成的非正式用词，义为「像海星的」

senses.title: A star-shaped sea animal
senses.definition: a flat sea animal with five or more arms that lives on the seabed and creeps along with tiny tube feet
senses.definitionCN: 一种身体扁平、有五个或更多腕足的海洋动物，生活在海床，靠微小的管足缓慢移动
senses.example: At the aquarium, a starfish slowly crossed the glass tank.
senses.exampleCN: 在水族馆里，一只海星慢慢爬过玻璃缸。
senses.why: English joins star and fish, so the name is simply a fish-shaped thing that looks like a star.
senses.whyCN: 英语把 star 与 fish 拼在一起，所以名字就是「长得像星星、又被称为鱼的东西」。

senses.title: Its pattern or shape
senses.definition: a star-shaped pattern or design copied from the five arms of the animal
senses.definitionCN: 仿照海星五条腕足设计的星形图案
senses.example: The children cut a starfish pattern from blue paper.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用蓝纸剪出海星形状的图案。
senses.why: Once the animal is known, its unmistakable outline becomes a handy name for any five-pointed shape.
senses.whyCN: 人们熟悉这种动物之后，它醒目的轮廓就成了任何五角形状的现成说法。

senses.title: Starfish that lose an arm
senses.definition: a starfish that can grow a new arm or a new body after part of it is lost
senses.definitionCN: 在失去部分身体后能重新长出新腕足甚至新身体的海星
senses.example: Many starfish can regrow an arm within a few months.
senses.exampleCN: 许多海星能在几个月内重新长出腕足。
senses.why: The star shape suggests a whole that can be rebuilt from any single piece, so regeneration became part of the everyday idea of a starfish.
senses.whyCN: 星形让人想到整体可以由任何一块重新拼回来，于是再生能力成了海星日常印象的一部分。

senses.title: Starfish in sport and models
senses.definition: a posture with arms and legs spread wide, or a decorative object shaped like the animal
senses.definitionCN: 四肢大张的姿势，或做成海星形状的装饰品
senses.example: The gymnast landed in a starfish position on the mat.
senses.exampleCN: 体操运动员如同一只海星般伏在垫子上落地。
senses.why: The five spread arms are a ready-made picture of a body opened out, so the word stretches from nature to display and sport.
senses.whyCN: 五条摊开的腕足本身就是「身体完全张开」的现成图像，所以这个词从自然界延伸到陈列品和体育动作。

intro.en: Starfish is a plain English compound that simply calls the star-shaped sea animal a star and a fish, like shell-fish and cray-fish.
intro.cn: starfish 是朴素的英语复合词，把这种星形海洋动物直接叫作「星星」加「鱼」，与 shell-fish、cray-fish 的造词方式相同。

items.en: Star names anything that radiates from a centre, and fish was a loose word for nearly anything living in water.
items.cn: star 指从中心向外放射的任何东西，fish 则被宽泛地用来指几乎任何水中生物。

items.en: Forms such as starefish and sterrefish are recorded for the five-armed sea animal.
items.cn: 指这种五腕足海洋动物的 starefish、sterrefish 等拼写有记录。

items.en: The spelling starfish settles into the shape we use today.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，拼写定型为今天的 starfish。

items.en: Marine biology borrows the compound for the whole family of such animals.
items.cn: 十九世纪海洋生物学借用这个词指称这一大类动物。

items.en: The date of first use is recorded with certainty, but the separate parts keep their ordinary senses of star and fish.
items.cn: 首次使用的年代有明确记载，但两个成分仍保持 star 与 fish 的普通含义。

note.en: Starfish shares its shape and habitat with other spiny sea animals, and shares its spelling link with star and sea.
note.cn: starfish 在形状和栖息环境上与其他带刺的海生动物相邻，在拼写上则与 star、sea 相联。

entries.definition: a bright point of light in the night sky
entries.definitionCN: 夜空中的亮点，starfish 的前半部分，与拼写并非整体借用

entries.definition: an animal that lives in water and has fins
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水里、有鳍的动物，starfish 的后半部分

entries.definition: a small star, or a young actor
entries.definitionCN: 小星星或年轻演员，与 starfish 共享 star 这一成分

entries.definition: the biological name for the same animal, used because it is not a fish
entries.definitionCN: 同一种动物的生物学名称，因为海星其实不是鱼

entries.definition: a small round sea animal covered with long spines
entries.definitionCN: 海胆，体表布满长刺的小型海生动物

entries.definition: a soft round sea animal with long trailing arms
entries.definitionCN: 水母，身体柔软、拖着长触手的海洋动物

normalIntro.en: Starfish is a compound anyone can read at a glance: a star plus a fish.
normalIntro.cn: starfish 是一眼看懂的复合词：一颗星加一条鱼。

normal.en: Star means a star shape, and fish here just means a water animal, not a true fish.
normal.cn: star 表星形，fish 这里只指水中生物，并不是真正的鱼。

normal.en: The same relaxing use of fish appears in jellyfish and crayfish.
normal.cn: fish 的这种宽松用法同样出现在 jellyfish 和 crayfish 里。

normal.en: Scientific writing prefers the neutral sea star for the same animal.
normal.cn: 科技写作更常用中性的 sea star 指同一种动物。

normal.en: The arms are called rays, so a five-armed starfish has five rays.
normal.cn: 海星的腕足在英文里叫 ray，所以五腕海星有五条 ray。

normal.en: A starfish-shaped biscuit keeps the hyphens, just as the derivative starfish-shaped does.
normal.cn: starfish-shaped biscuit 保留连字符，派生词 starfish-shaped 也是如此。

abstract.en: Picture a chocolate-brown star lying still on wet rock at low tide.
abstract.cn: 想象退潮时，一枚巧克力色的星星静静趴在湿岩上。

abstract.en: Think of five slow fingers pulling the body forward by a few millimetres a minute.
abstract.cn: 想象五根缓慢的手指，从身体下伸出来抓住地面，每分钟只挪动几毫米。

abstract.en: See one arm split off and grow into a whole new star.
abstract.cn: 想象一条腕足断落后，重新长成一颗完整的新星。

examples.en: A starfish can regrow an arm that a predator has bitten off.
examples.cn: 海星能把被天敌咬掉的腕足重新长出来。

examples.en: The tidal pool held two starfish and a crowd of small crabs.
examples.cn: 潮池里有两只海星和一群小螃蟹。

examples.en: Schoolchildren drew a starfish with five fat arms on the classroom wall.
examples.cn: 小学生在教室墙上画了一只长着五条胖腕足的海星。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯塔菲什」——拆开看就是「星星」加「鱼」，想象一条鱼长成五角星；这是拆词联想，词源上它只是英语把 star 与 fish 拼成的复合词。

root: 英语 star（星）+ fish（水中生物）复合而成，最早见于十六世纪，并非外来词；fish 的用法很宽松，jellyfish、crayfish 同理。

sensesIntro.en: Starfish starts as the everyday name of the animal, then borrows its outline for shapes and its splitting body for ideas of rebuilding.
sensesIntro.cn: starfish 先是这种动物的日常称呼，再借用它的轮廓指星形，最后用它能断腕重生的身体引向「重建」的联想。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a five-armed star pressed flat against the sea floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚五条腕足的星星平贴在海床上。

branches.en: The animal itself is the base sense.
branches.cn: 动物本身是基础义项。

branches.en: The outline turns into a pattern.
branches.cn: 动物轮廓转化为图案义项。

branches.en: Regrowth after injury is the living sense.
branches.cn: 受伤后再生是活体义项。

branches.en: Arms spread wide give both the display object and the body posture.
branches.cn: 张开的腕足同时引出装饰造型与身体姿势。

branches.en: Shapes and postures both borrow the five-point look.
branches.cn: 图案与姿势都借用了正五角的外观。

intro.en: Starfish is built from two ordinary English words, star and fish, so it has almost no affixes of its own; related forms simply attach hyphens or suffixes.
intro.cn: starfish 由两个普通英语单词 star 与 fish 构成，本身几乎没有词缀；相关形式只是加连字符或后缀。

latinIntro.en: Starfish has no Latin root; biology borrowed it for sea stars whose scientific family names such as Asterias come from Greek for star.
latinIntro.cn: starfish 没有拉丁词根；生物学借用它指海星类，其科属学名如 Asterias 则来自希腊语的「星」。

items.meaning: a bright point of light, or a star shape
items.example: Star gives the name its five pointed arms.
items.exampleCN: star 给这个名字带来五角的形状。

items.example: Fish here means a water animal rather than a true fish.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 fish 指水中生物，而非真正的鱼。

items.example: Starfish is the everyday compound name.
items.exampleCN: starfish 是日常复合名称。

items.example: The suffix -shaped forms starfish-shaped.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -shaped 构成 starfish-shaped。

items.meaning: having the form of a star
items.example: Starfish-shaped describes a biscuit or a pool.
items.exampleCN: starfish-shaped 形容星形饼干或水池。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the rare noun starfishing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成少见的 starfishing。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the informal starfishy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成非正式的 starfishy。

items.meaning: star or star shape used before another word
items.example: The combining form star- also gives starlet.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 star- 也构成 starlet。
